danish_heritage: Denmark's long naval traditions and its mastery of maritime logistics culminated in major dockyards like those in Copenhagen. As Scandinavia, we inherit these powerful infrastructures and traditions, boosting our diplomatic standing and naval readiness.
finnish_heritage: The Finnish cavalry — Hakkapeliitta — gained a fearsome reputation in wars in Europe These riders, raised in the wild forests and plains of Finland, bring experience, adaptability, and toughness to our ranks. By formalizing their role, we will create a permanent elite force within our armies.
swedish_roots: From the disciplined Carolean ranks to the strong freeholding peasantry, Sweden's military prowess is an essential pillar of Scandinavia. By integrating Swedish institutions and recruitment systems, we reinforce the manpower and strength of our empire.
sko_fulani_expansion: For too long the people of Western Africa have labored under rulers that, while professing to be righteous, indulged in syncretism. No more! Our flag shall always fly above that of worldly kingdoms!
sko_recruit_the_faithful: Everyone who is ready to serve under our righteous leaders must be welcome, regardless of their heritage.
sko_education_for_all: By encouraging the spread of literacy and scholarship among men and women alike, we can advance our society and further our hold over our lands. The family of our rulers must have a special place in these efforts, serving as an ideal to emulate.
sko_religious_court: Instead of displaying the worldly pomp of our rule, our court should focus on spiritual matters. By inviting learned religious figures to teach in our capital, we can show our true commitment to our faith.
sko_recruit_fulani_generals: The Fulbe people are distinguished warriors, serving as leaders in all corners of Western Africa. We should establish ourselves as a permanent employer for their most capable commanders.
sko_one_people_in_faith: Our lands are home to many people of different cultures and languages. We must emphasize our faith as the unifying force, joining all people under one banner.
diocese_of_smolensk: Once a spiritual stronghold of Orthodox Christianity and home to one of the oldest bishoprics in the region, the Diocese of Smolensk embodies our people's unshakable faith.
smolenskian_resolve: For centuries, Smolensk has been a land carved up by outsiders — Lithuanian dukes, Polish kings, and Muscovite princes. To survive, we clung to what united us: our faith and our fortitude. If we are ever to rise again, we must cast off divisions and rally around the sacred idea that, above all, there is only Smolensk.
link_the_steppes_trade: Positioned between forest and steppe, Smolensk has long been a crossroads of war and commerce. By improving overland infrastructure and securing the arteries of caravan travel, we can reforge our role as the vital hinge between northern Rus', the Baltic, and the southern trade routes of the steppes.
hub_of_militarism: Long has war defined our fate, but now it shall define our strength. From the ruinous embrace of warfare and siege, Smolensk rises as a center of military production — cannons, firearms, powder and doctrine flow outward from our armories. Let the world see us not as a prize to be taken, but as a hammer to be feared, ready to strike the anvil of foreign conquerors.
armories_of_smolensk: After decades of warfare on every border, we learned to fight with weapons of both east and west. Blending Muscovite grit with western precision, our armories now produce elite artillery and tactics unmatched by our rivals. From our forges comes firepower — and from firepower, domination and perseverance.
tws_unified_legal_code: The territories which constitute our land have suffered revolts due to unjust applications of laws. In order to prevent these occurrences in the future, we should standardize our legal code and ensure our laws are applied fairly. This will surely prevent any uprising from spiraling into chaos.
tws_ensure_loyal_families: The Noble Families of both Sicilies exert much power in our stead. By granting them prestigious yet meaningless roles at court, we will ensure their loyalty and guarantee stable rule over our countryside.
tws_revitalize_the_lands: Previous rulers put too much focus on particular areas of our country. If we want to retain control of both Sicilies, we will have to invest equally and fairly in both parts. One step towards this goal is attracting people to settle in previously neglected areas.
tws_oversea_ambitions: Expanding our territories within Italy is a difficult task, navigating a treacherous web of alliances and risking the anger of the Pope himself. Therefore, we should look overseas, where potential riches await us in the lands of northern Africa and Greece.
tws_capable_vicars: A particular struggle of our unified country is governing both sides of the Strait of Messina. Since our ruler can only be present on one side at a time, the other will have to be given to a vicar, ruling in our name. We must be sure to appoint only the most capable and trustworthy people to this vital role to prevent corruption.
tws_protect_the_coastline: Our coastline is vast, and vulnerable to raids by pirates hunting for slaves. We need to establish a navy to patrol, protect, and eventually defeat this vile threat to our people.
usa_mayflower_compact: Bound together by shared peril and purpose, the early settlers drafted a pact of self-governance. Even in the wilderness, the seeds of society and compromise found soil.
usa_empowered_assemblies: Elected assemblies emerged throughout the colonies, empowering landowners to govern themselves. The humble origins of liberty lie in the halls of these institutions.
usa_great_awakening: A wave of religious revival sweeps the land, challenging old authorities and stirring the moral conscience of a rising people.
usa_declaration_of_independence:
We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal.

With this bold declaration, we shall break the chains of subjugation, and embraced our shared destiny!
usa_bill_of_rights: ...or abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press; or the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.
usa_recognized_sovereignty: Treaties and diplomacy affirmed what our struggles have earned. Our place on the stage of diplomacy is no longer questioned, but respected.
usa_era_good_feelings: In the wake of hardship, peace and unity have brought a rare moment of national harmony. The people flourish with optimism and order.
adu_khilafa_qurtuba_renewed: Our restoration of the Ḵilāfat Qurṭuba, the Caliphate of Córdoba, revives the ceremonial titulature of 'Abd ar-Raḥmān III, complete with the throne hall of the rebuilt Madīnat az-Zahrā, the gold thread ṭirāz robes embroidered with the caliph's regnal year, and the Friday sermon proclaimed once more in the great mosque of Córdoba. We strike new dinars from West African gold in the name of the renewed caliph, send investiture banners to the Maghrebi sultans who acknowledge our suzerainty, and accept embassies from the Mamlūks of Cairo as equals rather than petitioners. This caliphal authority formalizes the ḏimma covenant over Córdoba's numerous Christian and Jewish subjects, binding the peninsula's diverse populations into a single project that no regional Maghrebi dynasty can easily contest.
adu_yusufiyya_andalusiyya: The Yūsufiyya Andalusiyya (our network of royal madrasas built on the fourteenth-century Granadan model of Yūsuf I) establishes endowed teaching mosques at Córdoba, Seville, Toledo, Valencia, and Zaragoza, each provided with a library, a hospice, and a faculty drawn from across the Islamic world. Our scholars synthesize Andalusi Mālikī jurisprudence with the Ash'arī theology of Cairo and the philosophical revival of the Avicennan tradition imported from Persia. This state-funded learning produces a literate clergy and a class of trained jurists whose loyalty to the restored state is bound directly to the offices it endows.
adu_riba_al_andalus: Our long-distance commerce (the Ribā al-'Andalus, the commercial routes of the western Mediterranean) knits Genoese, Catalan, Maghrebi, and Mamlūk markets together through Andalusi merchant houses operating out of Almería, Málaga, Cádiz, and Tangier. Letters of credit drawn in our gold dinar circulate as far as Alexandria and Bruges, and Andalusi Jewish and Mozarab financiers underwrite trade ventures the older Christian banks would consider too risky to touch. This web of credit and commerce lets us borrow on easier terms and taxes every kind of trade that crosses Iberian waters.
adu_aman_ahl_al_dhimma: Our renewed pact of protection, the Amān Ahl aḏ-Ḏimma, extends formal safeguards to the Christian and Jewish communities of the restored state, regulating their churches and synagogues, their internal courts, and the jizya they pay in lieu of military service. Mudéjar and Mozarab guilds receive royal charters confirming their crafts, while the great Sephardic financial houses re-establish branches in Córdoba and Granada under sultanate protection. This convivencia binds the productive non-Muslim communities into the life of the state and turns the diversity of our cities into a source of prosperity rather than rebellion.
adu_armada_andalusiyya: The Armāda Andalusiyya, our combined armada, fuses the state navy at Almería and Cádiz with the chartered corsair fleets of Salé, Tetuán, and the Andalusi exile captains operating from Algiers, producing a single command capable of contesting the western Mediterranean against any peer Christian power. The fleet's amphibious doctrine combines squadrons of galleys and sailing ships with embarked marine columns trained for rapid descents on enemy coasts and rapid re-embarkation under fire. This integrated naval force lets our armies project across the Strait of Gibraltar and along the African littoral faster than any opposing fleet can intercept.
adu_nahda_andalusiyya: Our modern revival, the Nahḍa Andalusiyya, opens with the recovered manuscripts of Ibn Rushd and az-Zahrāwī printed at the restored presses of Córdoba, gathers around the new Royal Academy of Granada under scholars in the lineage of Pascual de Gayangos and Reinhart Dozy, and flowers in the bilingual Arabic-Castilian literary journals of the late nineteenth century. We translate the new European scientific works into modern Arabic and recover the medieval Andalusi corpus from the Escorial, the Bodleian, and the libraries of Fez and Tunis. This intellectual renaissance restores our state's standing as a center of Mediterranean learning and sustains the prestige of our court well past the age in which other monarchies must purchase theirs anew.
algerian_hilali_settlement: The Banū Hilāl and Banū Sulaym Arab clans push west out of Egypt across generations, settling among the Sanhaja and Zenata Berbers of the central Maghreb and imposing their dialect and tribal genealogies on the absorbed populations. Our shayḵs adopt the Hilāli kinship structures, our valleys are partitioned by negotiated arrangements over pasture and villages, and the older Berber tongues retreat into a substratum preserved only in pasture songs and place names. Blending Arab and Berber in this way gives the central Maghrebi Tell a tribal and genealogical order that sets our culture apart from the more inland zenati and kabyle highland identities.
alg_kasbah_citadel: Our fortress quarter, the qasba of Algiers perched on the hillside above the harbor with its honeycomb of narrow alleys and tightly built houses, provides the defensive seat from which every Algerian regime governs. Our resident garrisons hold the citadel against any landward or seaward attack, our cisterns store enough water and grain for an extended siege, and our gatekeepers control access to the upper city even when the lower harbor is held by an enemy. From its kasbah our state governs from a fortified seat that an enemy cannot easily take, unlike the more open Maghrebi coastal cities.
zab_sidi_okba_shrine: The tomb of 'Uqba ibn Nāfi' (founder of Kairouan, who led the first Arab armies into the Maghreb and is buried at our southern village of Sidi Okba) anchors a sacred pilgrimage site whose religious authority predates every dynasty of the Maghreb. Our resident shrine keepers maintain the tomb, our annual pilgrimage draws zawaya scholars and notables from across the western Islamic world, and our ulema invoke the founder's authority in legal opinions that bind clients far beyond our actual political reach. The founding shrine gives our state a sacred claim to legitimacy, ancient and tied to the prophetic conqueror himself.
alg_thaalibid_descent: Our dynasty, the Banū Tha'ālibī, traced through Sīdī 'Abd ar-Raḥmān ath-Tha'ālibī and his ancestors back to Idrīs II of Morocco and the Prophet's grandson Ḥasan, establishes a sharīfī lineage in the central Maghreb that no Berber dynasty can match for prophetic and genealogical authority. Our court genealogists certify the descent at each accession, our recital of the lineage at every bay'a ceremony binds the religious caste to the ruling family, and the consensus of our nobles and ulema around the sharifian claim survives every internal succession dispute. The sharifian descent of the original Algiers line gives it a sacred legitimacy rooted in genealogical fact, which a successor ruling Algiers as a mere state can never claim.
algerian_tell_wheatlands: The Tell-region plains of the Mitidja, the Chelif valley, the Soummam, and the rolling country south of Constantine produce the wheat harvests that feed our coastal cities and supply the central treasury through state-licensed export. The fellahin work the irrigated bottomlands under hereditary land tenure. At season's end cooperative threshing yards gather the harvest, and state-licensed grain warehouses bridge the bad years that the rainfed Tell occasionally suffers. Wheat for export fills the coffers of our cities as the more pastoral Maghrebi lands never could.
alg_algiers_emporium: Algiers emerges as the central coastal emporium of the central Maghreb. Merchants of Pisa, Genoa, Aragon, and Provence maintain resident factors in our harbor, and customs revenue from Christian trade rivals the income of the inland tribute. At the harbor front yards our shipwrights build both the coastal traders and the early war galleys that our captains crew. Our merchant guilds intermediate the wool, wax, leather, coral, and slaves that flow between the Tell hinterland and the Mediterranean markets, and our system of consuls and treaties grants formal residence and judicial protection to the visiting foreign factors. From this commercial emergence come the port revenue and the sailors on which the later corsair state is built.
zab_zibane_palmery: Our oasis belt, the Zībān palm gardens stretching from Biskra and Tolga through Sidi Okba and Bou Saada to Ouled Djellal, produces the dates that the Maghrebi and trans-Saharan markets specifically commission for their size, sweetness, and keeping qualities. Our orchard owners hold hereditary leases on individual palm plots, our irrigation guildsmen apportion well-water by ancient share tables, and our caravan masters price each consignment by origin grove and harvest year. The Zibane palm country supplies a luxury trade in dates that no broader fruit-growing region of the Maghreb can displace from the elite markets.
alg_thaalibid_emirate: The Tha'alibid emirate ruling Algiers, proclaimed under the religious and political authority of the Banū Tha'ālibī family and exercising state powers across the central Maghrebi coast from Cherchell to Dellys, maintains continuous diplomatic and commercial relations with the Aragonese, Genoese, and Hafsid neighbors that the later regency inherits in form if not in dynastic continuity. Our court chancellery exchanges sealed letters with the Christian powers under formal capitulations, and our ports admit foreign factors under negotiated residence rights. The sharifian titulature on our coinage distinguishes our rule from Zayyanid Tlemcen and Hafsid Tunis. As a pre-regency emirate, the original Algiers line holds a lasting claim to rule as a true state, a claim no successor government restores in the same dynastic terms.
algerian_carpet_weaving: Our Berber and Arab weavers, from the rug makers of Kalaa Beni Rashed and the Beni Mizab of the M'zab valley to the urban guilds of Algiers and Constantine, produce the geometric-patterned woolen rugs that the Mediterranean and trans-Saharan markets specifically commission for their distinct Maghrebi character. From the Tell flocks comes the wool our spinners work, while our dyers compound indigo, madder, and henna into the bold reds and blues that define the regional aesthetic. Knot weavers then execute patterns passed down through generations of master-apprentice transmission. Our carpets are prized across the Mediterranean for the variety of their patterns and the fastness of their colors, and the urban guilds grow rich on the export.
alg_corsair_emergence: The corsair tradition takes root in Algiers. Captains from across the Mediterranean settle in our harbor under state charter. Our shipwrights specialize in the fast classes of galley and galiot that the open water raiding war demands, and the captains' guild formalizes the prize distribution rules that turn private raiding into a state-organized industry. Our renegade Christian, Greek, and Italian captains serve alongside native rais; our markets re-export the captured cargoes and ransomed captives; and our crown takes its share of every successful prize. With the rise of the corsairs, Algiers builds a maritime war economy of its own, while the more agriculturally anchored Maghrebi rivals have nothing like them.
zab_saharan_terminus: Our oasis sits at the northern terminus of the western Saharan caravan corridor. Caravans from Touat, Touggourt, and the central Sahara converge on Biskra before continuing north to Constantine and Tunis or east into Hafsid territory, while our merchant houses provision the southbound legs with grain, cloth, salt, and pottery from the Tell. Our caravanserais host sub-Saharan, Berber, and Maghrebi traders side by side; our customs officers tax through traffic at modest rates that keep the corridor profitable; and our diplomatic letters bind the caravan route's contributing tribes to our chamber arbitration. This place at the end of the desert road makes our oasis a city of merchants and envoys, as no purely agricultural oasis could be.
alg_thaalibid_resistance: Our emirate resists the multiple foreign pressures bearing down on Algiers in the late medieval period: Spanish coastal raids and Cardinal Cisneros's expeditions, foreign corsair captains looking for a base under any pretext of religious solidarity, and the periodic Hafsid-Zayyanid neighbors seeking to incorporate us into their tributary networks. We retain seasoned mercenary and corsair companies whose upkeep our treasury has learned to bear, we press the siege against every foreign strongpoint planted on our coast, the Spanish-held Peñón foremost among them, and our diplomats negotiate the temporary truces that preserve our autonomous realm through each successive wave. From this martial tradition the original Algiers line passes down an inheritance of campaigning abroad, which the later regency, paradoxically, would take up and turn against the same powers.
algerian_makhzen_tribes: Our state-allied tribes, the Banū Hilāl-descended Bedouin confederations that historically aligned themselves with whichever Algerian polity could secure their pasture rights and grain supply, provide the light cavalry of our central forces and the inter-tribal contact network that no purely urban administration could replicate. Paramount-shayḵs hold formal court titles, and annual stipends bind tribal contingents to the state. Marriage alliances with notable tribal families secure recruiting catchments across the Tell. This makhzen system fills our armies with horsemen and binds the frontier tribes to us, as the more centralized Maghrebi rivals cannot.
alg_corsair_state_economy: The corsair state economy reaches its mature form. The crown licenses every prize taking captain and draws a fixed share of every successful raid. Our shipyards turn out the standard galley, galiot, and xebec classes that captains lease from the state on prize share terms. Our recruiting agents draw foreign captains and crews to our harbor with state-funded advances on the next prize cycle, our naval administration office tracks the war statuses of every Mediterranean power to direct the raiding effort, and our central treasury depends on the prize revenue cycle as much as on the flows of customs and tribute. This state-organized corsair economy fills our coffers with the spoils of war more steadily than the more conventional trading states of the Mediterranean can manage.
zab_foggara_irrigation: The foggāra underground channel system, qanats dug under the desert sand to bring water from upland water tables to the oasis gardens, gets extended and renewed under our oasis council coordination, freeing new cultivable land from the older surface irrigation perimeter. Our guild of foggara diggers passes the channel construction technique through hereditary apprenticeship, our resident villages contribute corvée-labor for the cleaning rotations, and our oasis chamber arbitrates the share water disputes that the new channels inevitably generate. As the foggara spread, our oasis gains more cultivable land and more people than the rival oases that rely on surface irrigation.
alg_native_restoration: Our dynasty, restored to the throne after the foreign officer interregnum and the upheavals that followed, reasserts the indigenous Algerian sovereignty that the original Tha'alibid line carried before its extinction. Our court re-establishes the diplomatic networks that the regency's chancellery had let lapse, and our envoys re-engage the Mediterranean and trans-Saharan powers under the restored sharifian legitimacy. Scholar historians produce the chronicles that justify the restoration as an unbroken line of legitimacy. The restoration renews the diplomatic reach of the original Algiers line, with an authority that successors resting on mere state power could not muster.
algerian_qadiriyya_expansion: The Qādiriyya tariqa, the older of our two great Sufi brotherhoods, traced through the Baghdadi line back to 'Abd al-Qādir al-Jīlānī, anchors the rural religious and judicial authority across the Tell and the steppe frontier. Our zawiyas train Quranic scholars in remote village mosques, our shayḵs mediate the inter-tribal disputes that no urban qadi could settle by force of law alone, and our lodges provide the loyalty oath networks that bind frontier tribes to their patron brotherhood. This rural anchor lets the brotherhood mediate in matters of doctrine and law where purely urban courts cannot reach.
alg_consolidated_deylik: The deylik settles into a stable political order: the dey rules from the Janina palace, the provincial beys remit tribute and troops, the Janissary corps stands as the army, and the corsair captains' guild keeps its voice in his election. After generations of coups and rotating officers, the treasury, the prize licensing office, and the diplomatic offices at last run from a single Bardo-palace bureaucracy. A consolidated deylik runs our state with an order that the old rotating officer governance could never sustain.
zab_biskra_fair: The annual Biskra autumn fair, convening Saharan caravans from Touat, Sahel merchants from Constantine, sub-Saharan slave traders from the Niger bend, and Bedouin pastoralists from the steppe fringe, turns our oasis capital into a regional commercial hub for the autumn weeks. Pavilions host the negotiations. The customs house weighs and registers every transaction, and the merchant guild posts standard scales and assay weights to which all participants must conform. The Biskra fair draws the caravans together at set times and turns their natural meeting point into a market the state manages and taxes.
alg_thaalibid_sultanate: Our dynasty, elevated to sultanate status as the restored Algerian realm matures into a fully sovereign state, claims the same titulature and ceremonial protocol that the Hafsid and Marinid sovereigns wielded, distinguished from the Janissary-promoted deylik form by the unbroken dynastic and genealogical continuity that no rotating officer regime can match. At the Bardo-equivalent palace our court stages the formal accession ceremonies, and our scholars compile the sultanate's claim to sovereignty in juridical commentaries. A consensus of nobles binds the polity through dynastic loyalty rather than corps election. Thus the original Algiers line rules in a form that fits its sharifian claim to legitimacy, as the dey regency, rooted in Janissary promotion, never could.
algerian_tijaniyya_birth: The Tijāniyya tariqa, founded by Aḥmad at-Tijānī in 'Ayn Māḍī in the central Algerian steppe, emerges as a uniquely Algerian-soil Sufi order with a distinctive doctrine of the silsila of light and a fast-spreading network of branch zawiyas across the Maghreb. Our founder receives his initiating vision in the Algerian desert, our first sister lodges open in Fez and Tlemcen as the order spreads westward, and our scholars publish the doctrinal compendia that define the brotherhood's distinctive practices. With the Tijāniyya, our culture can boast a Sufi order born on our own soil, a distinction no other Maghrebi culture claims for the period.
alg_consular_relations: Our system of consular relations, with formal consulates from every major Mediterranean and Atlantic power resident in Algiers, periodic treaty renewals with each, and the customary arrangements of gifts and payments that accompany them, manages the state's relations with rivals more powerful than any single defeat could humble. The dey audiences the consular delegations on a fixed protocol. Our chancellery files the running correspondence in multiple languages, and our customs office administers the differential tariffs that each treaty state's merchants enjoy. With its consuls and treaties, Algiers deals flexibly with the many foreign powers of the modern age, while the more isolated North African states stand alone.
zab_rahmaniyya_expansion: The Raḥmāniyya tariqa, founded by Sīdī Muḥammad ibn 'Abd ar-Raḥmān al-Azharī in the central Kabyle region and expanding southward through the Aurès foothills, establishes branch zawiyas across our oasis belt over the course of generations. Our resident shayḵs accept Raḥmāniyya initiation, our scholar families take students from the Kabyle and Algerian centers, and our merchant pilgrims maintain the correspondence across regions that binds the order's scattered lodges into one religious network. Through the Raḥmāniyya lodges, students and shayḵs pass freely between our oasis and the central Algerian highlands.
alg_thaalibid_revival: Our reformist circles revive the Tha'alibid heritage as the ideological and cultural anchor of the modern Algerian state, invoking the centuries before the Janissary interregnum when an indigenous sharifian dynasty governed central Algeria with continuous diplomatic and commercial engagement with the Mediterranean world. Pamphleteers publish the Tha'alibid chronicles in modern Arabic editions, and schoolmasters teach the early modern Algerian history alongside the Maghrebi-wide canonical narrative. Around the Sīdī 'Abd ar-Raḥmān shrine in Algiers, scholar circles maintain the unbroken religious and cultural authority that no political extinction could fully erase. The Tha'alibid revival gives the original Algiers line a heritage and an ideology of its own, which modernization movements built on state power alone lack.
aragonese_montaneses: The high Pyrenean valleys around Jaca and Sobrarbe have forged a hardy population of mountain warriors known as the Montañeses, whose long descent from the foothills gave our kingdom its earliest military reputation in the Reconquista. Trained from youth to fight on broken ground and accustomed to long winter campaigns, our highlanders move faster and strike harder than the lowland levies that have always opposed them. From these valleys come the mobile infantry whose endurance shapes every campaign we undertake.
ara_conquest_of_the_ebro: The descent from the Pyrenean valleys onto the plain of the Ebro crowns generations of frontier war: Huesca falls in 1096, and Alfonso el Batallador storms Zaragoza in 1118 to make it the seat of the kingdom. Our light frontier foot soldiers, hardened in the long march south and skilled in the reduction of walled Moorish towns, turns each captured stronghold into a base for the next advance. Our soldiery are built for taking fortresses, not for the sea.
ara_desperta_ferro: Desperta Ferro! (Awake Iron!) is the war cry of the Almogavars, accompanied by the striking of lance shafts and darts against flint to draw sparks before the charge. The cry was heard at the conquest of Mallorca under James I in 1229, on the slopes of the Bosphorus under Roger de Flor's Catalan Company, and in every Aragonese campaign of the long Mediterranean century. This battlefield ritual binds our infantry into a single chanting mass before contact, producing a shock effect that has unnerved Byzantines, Sicilians, and French alike.
aragonese_pyrenean_passes: The high passes of the central Pyrenees (Somport, Roncesvalles, and the lower seasonal trails) funnel every wagon load of Béarnais wool, Gascon wine, and Languedocian cloth that crosses into our markets, and our toll stations at Jaca and Canfranc have collected the Crown's share of that flow since the eleventh century. By improving the roads, garrisoning the watchtowers, and standardizing customs assessments along these Caminos Reales, we transform an accident of geography into a commercial monopoly. This control over the Pyrenean transit routes draws merchants from both sides of the mountains to our fairs and keeps the Crown's treasury supplied with reliable transit fees.
ara_a_mediterranean_trade_power: From the dynastic union of Aragon and the County of Barcelona in 1164, our Crown has built a Mediterranean commercial system anchored on Barcelona, Valencia, and Palma. The Consolat de Mar, the world's first standing maritime trade tribunal, adjudicates disputes from Pisa to Famagusta under Catalan law, and our consuls hold writ in every major port from Alexandria to Bruges. This commercial and legal system makes the Crown of Aragon the indispensable middleman between Italian banks, African gold, and Levantine spices.
ara_dinero_jaques: Minted at Jaca since the first kings of Aragon, the dinero jaqués becomes the trusted coin of the kingdom, its silver content guarded by the Cortes against every royal temptation to debase it. A sound currency lets the crown borrow cheaply, the merchants reckon honestly, and the treasury may collect its revenues without the friction of clipped and doubtful coin. This monetary stability underwrites the kingdom's finances more reliably than any single tax.
aragonese_castillos_frontera: The frontier between our kingdom and al-'Andalus is studded with Castillos de la Frontera: Loarre, Monzón, Albarracín, and dozens of lesser keeps perched on every defensible ridge. Each fortress is maintained at the expense of the local commune, with the Crown contributing only walls and a captain, producing a defensive network that no invader can easily breach without costly siegework. This system makes our territory disproportionately expensive to invade and bleeds any attacking force long before our field armies need to give battle.
ara_diputacion_del_general: Our kingdom's standing executive, the Diputación del General, emerges from the Cortes of Monzón as a permanent commission that administers the general subsidio, defends the realm's fueros between Cortes sessions, and represents the four estates in continuous dialogue with the Crown. We will channel the kingdom's tax revenue through the Diputación's accounting offices, fund public works through its commissions, and lodge the noble houses' grievances in its standing chamber. Because the Diputación never adjourns, our realm keeps its parliamentary memory and its accounts in order, while the Crown's other realms must start afresh each session.
ara_overseas_realms: Beyond the sea the Crown gathers a constellation of realms (Sicily won in 1282, Sardinia in 1324, and Naples under Alfonso el Magnánimo) each kept as a distinct kingdom under a viceroy rather than absorbed. We bind these realms to the dynasty with confirmed privileges, native magistracies, and a light hand on their liberties, so that their nobilities find more profit in loyalty than in revolt. This federation of overseas crowns yields the dynasty a steady tribute and a chain of Mediterranean bases no rival can easily prise loose.
aragonese_salinas_reales: Our Crown has long claimed monopoly over the salt-producing valleys of Naval, Sallent, and Remolinos, contracting their extraction to royal officers who answer directly to the treasury. The Salinas Reales provide a steady income that supplements the unpredictable agrarian taxes and gives our state the liquid capital to weather lean harvests. This mineral revenue makes our government uniquely solvent and frees us from constant dependence on the Cortes for emergency funds.
ara_carinena_vineyards: The stony terraces of Cariñena and Campo de Borja, baked by the dry interior sun and swept by the cierzo wind, yield a dark, powerful wine prized far beyond the kingdom. Monastic cellars and town guilds expand the plantings across the Ebro depression, and the vintage travels by river and mule to the courts and garrisons of the crown. This robust viticulture turns thin upland soil into one of the inland kingdom's most valuable and durable exports.
ara_stronger_united: Since forming the dynastic union with the County of Barcelona in 1164, the Crown has functioned as a composite monarchy in which each component realm (Aragon proper, Catalonia, Valencia, Mallorca, and Sardinia) preserves its own Corts, fueros, and currency. To strengthen central administration without abolishing these liberties, we will rationalize the chancery, standardize royal tax collection across the realms, and reinforce the office of the Lloctinent General, who governs in the absence of the king. This administrative consolidation lets the Crown coordinate war, taxation, and diplomacy with a speed that no other composite monarchy in Europe can match.
aragonese_sociedad_economica: The Real Sociedad Económica Aragonesa de Amigos del País, founded in Zaragoza, gathers our enlightened citizens (clergy, nobles, and burghers alike) to debate agricultural improvement, manufacturing, and commercial reform. Its meetings spread practical knowledge through pamphlets, prize competitions, and direct correspondence with reformers across Europe. This network of patriotic improvers raises the productivity of every sector its members touch and transforms our province into one of Iberia's quietest engines of modernization.
ara_basilica_del_pilar: At Zaragoza rises the great baroque Basílica del Pilar, raised over the pillar where tradition holds the Virgin appeared to Saint James, drawing pilgrims from across the Spains. The crown endows its chapter, processes beneath its towers on the great feasts, and wraps its legitimacy in the most venerable Marian devotion of the peninsula. This sacral prestige binds clergy and commons to the dynasty and sanctifies the kingdom's rule as no mere law could.
ara_protection_of_the_little_folk: Decades of campaigns from Lepanto to the Catalan Revolt have left thousands of widows, orphans, and crippled veterans of the Tercios de Aragón dependent on parish charity. The Crown will fund a system of Casas de Misericordia and orphanage workshops in Zaragoza, Valencia, and Barcelona, where the children of fallen soldiers receive food, schooling, and apprenticeships under royal patronage. This visible care for soldiers' families restores recruiting enthusiasm in towns that had grown weary of seeing their sons march off and never return.
aragonese_foralism: After several decrees stripped our kingdom of its medieval institutions, a persistent movement of jurists, historians, and provincial nobles have worked to preserve the memory and practical force of the lost fueros. The Foralist cause draws on regional identity to negotiate with the central government for restored privileges, regional courts, and recognition of distinct legal customs. Our steady pressure keeps Madrid from treating our province as one more uniform administrative unit, and our institutions outlive every reorganization the Bourbons attempt.
ara_gunpowder_souls: The Valencian Fallas (annual neighborhood festivals built around enormous wood-and-papier-mâché monuments burned with fireworks on the feast of Saint Joseph) have produced an entire artisan class skilled in the handling of black powder, fuse mixing, and pyrotechnic timing. The same workshops that fabricate spectacular Saint Joseph crowns now produce ranging tables, fuze set artillery shells, and the explosive bouquet rounds adopted by the royal arsenal. Festival-born expertise has grown into a homegrown gunpowder engineering tradition, one that mid-sized European powers must buy from German or French specialists.
ara_zaragoza_industry: Zaragoza and the towns of the Ebro corridor fill with sugar refineries, flour mills, foundries, and rail workshops as the inland kingdom enters the industrial age. The Imperial Canal's water, the new lines linking the city to the Cantabrian coast and the Mediterranean, and a steady migration off the land feed a growing manufacturing economy. This industrial awakening lifts the once-agrarian heartland into a producing region rivaling the old coastal centers.
ayu_prestigious_cavalry: Whether on horseback or atop an elephant, we can boast of an impressive cavalry, usually made up of descendants from the most prestigious families. Their contributions through supporting our infantry are invaluable.
ayu_white_elephant: The white elephant symbolizes sacred kingship in Buddhism tradition, and is also the emblem of our ruler. Possessing a white elephant legitimizes our authority, proving to our subjects that we rule with the blessing of the divine.
ayu_ayutthaya_literature: Our country has a rich and complex literary tradition, from the epic Lilit poems narrating famous military conflicts, to the Nirat poetry of travels and lost lovers; from folk legend of local heroes to panegyrics praising the feats of our most glorious rulers.
ayu_phrai_luang: All freemen subject to phrai service not only serve in war — the Phrai Thaan — but also assist in the construction of public works, at the discretion of local governors.
ayu_phrai_thaan: All males at the age of eighteen are to be registered with the military, and their information passed on to the government bureaucracy. Every male citizen is eligible to be conscripted and made to serve in the army in war, and we will make sure that they do so if needed.
ayu_floating_rice: Rice has been grown in our country for centuries, but the constant flooding of our rivers has always been an issue for its proper cultivation. This new variety of rice, used to growing in flooded conditions, will provide us with a stable source of food even when the rivers overflow.
ayu_sakdina: Our society is strictly organized along the Sakdina system. Each person knows their proper place in society and how much wealth and property they are entitled to have. This organization makes it much more efficient to extract taxes from them.
ayu_cosmopolitan_trade: Our country is home to many people from afar, who came here hoping to profit from the richness of our land. Having so many people and goods flowing through our borders is something we derive numerous benefits from.
network_of_cities: Across lakes and valleys, our cities bind themselves through roads, markets, and shared purpose, strengthening our reach.
status_by_merit: Warriors and nobles rise through valor and service, ensuring authority belongs to those who have truly earned it.
expansion_merchant_guilds: Pochtēcah merchants extend their routes far beyond our lands, enriching every marketplace loyal to the Mexihcah.
centralized_city_governance: The refomation of our government, in an attempt to support the sprawl of our newly-attained urban territories, shall be united under firm oversight, creating a more orderly and dependable administration.
wealth_of_mesoamerica: The fertile soils, forests, and mines of Ānāhuac yield immense riches, sustaining our growth and imperial ambitions. Properly utilizing these resources will bolster our affluence.
study_european_colonizers: Strangers have made contact with our people. Their unfamiliar ships and weapons instill awe and fear. Understanding their methods may be the key to survival.
new_fire_ceremonies: Once every fifty-two years, the world is renewed by flame, uniting the people in faith and cosmic balance.
sun_must_rise: Through devotion and ritual, we keep the sun's journey alive, easing the hearts and strengthening the spirit of our people. The preservation of equilibrium, and even the world, rests upon our shoulders.
bos_cultural_customs: Our people practice unique customs that transcend religious differences. The construction of stećci, elaborately decorated tombstones, is a tradition shared by all of us, regardless of faith. These distinctive monuments mark our lands as uniquely Bosnian.
bos_land_of_many_churches: Bosnia is home to several faiths. Not only is our land shared between the Orthodox and Catholic Churches, but it is also home to the South Slavic Christian faithful, the Krstjani. Isolated from central supervision, we will have to foster a local understanding and harmony between these different groups to maintain our stability.
bos_katun_communities: Parts of our population are organized into self-governing, pastoralist communities. Instead of bending them to a central government's will, we should cooperate with them, and in doing so try to extract more resources from our more remote areas.
bos_influence_of_the_stanak: Our nobility regularly gathers together to discuss the most pressing issues for our country. These meetings ensure our noble lords are aligned in their policies and show unity during our parliament sessions.
bos_defiant_terrain: Bosnia is a land of forested hills and mountains, cut through by river valleys. This terrain lends itself naturally to delaying and tiring invading armies, and we should use this to our advantage. Engaging our enemy only when it benefits us and letting the hostile terrain itself claim both their supplies and troops will preserve our strength.
bos_kingly_ambitions: The achievements and hard work of our people deserve recognition and protection. We will establish a prestigious title for ourselves and thereby secure that recognition from neighboring rulers, formalizing our status through diplomatic bonds.
bosnian_bosancica: The Bosnian people have unified around Bosančica, a unique, cursive Cyrillic script used for everything from diplomatic treaties to private merchant ledgers. This national script serves as a powerful cultural gatekeeper; it is difficult for foreigners to read but universal among the literate class, regardless of their specific confession. By maintaining this distinct script, the people ensure that their legal and historical records remain a 'closed book' to imperial administrators, preserving the secret nuances of property law and lineage in a format that reinforces their unique Slavic heritage.
bos_the_srebrenica_mint_office: As the mines of Srebrenica become the premier source of bullion in the Balkans, the realm has moved beyond the mere export of raw ore. We have established a Royal Mint and an Assay Office to regulate the purity of Bosnian silver, producing a coin which rivals those of Venice in reliability. By mandating that all silver extracted by Ragusan or Saxon miners be processed through state-controlled refineries, we capture a massive share of the value-added profit. This liquid wealth allows us to make Bosnia the most financially solvent power in the Dinaric Alps.
bosnian_people_from_the_hills: The geography of the Bosnian heartland is a vertical maze of limestone ridges and valleys that defy conventional mapping. Our people have adapted to this logic, mastering the secrets of the subterranean cavern networks and the logistics of the mule train.
bos_bosnian_ljekaruse: In the secluded valleys of our nation, monks of our monasteries have compiled the Ljekaruše, extensive medicinal codices written in the native Bosančica script. By synthesizing ancient Greco-Byzantine theory with the high-altitude herbalism of the Dinaric Alps, these manuals provide a sophisticated system of community healthcare in an era where professional physicians are a rarity. This mastery of folk medicine and surgery ensures our population remains resilient against the plagues that devastate the lowlands, fostering a cultural identity defined by intellectual self-reliance and the preservation of Slavic scientific knowledge.
bosnian_susjedsvto_of_bosnia: The ancient cultural concept of Susjedstvo (the sacred social obligation to protect and honor one's neighbor) has evolved into a sophisticated civic philosophy that transcends religious divides. In the face of external pressures, this unwritten code mandates that a neighbor's safety and property are as sacred as one's own. This practice prevents the 'Divide and Rule' tactics often used by foreign powers to incite internal strife. By prioritizing local solidarity and the 'Law of the Neighborhood', we maintain a level of social harmony and internal stability that allows the nation to present a single, unbreakable front against any attempt to dismantle our shared homeland.
bos_the_filigree_guilds: Drawing on the inexhaustible silver veins of the central mountains, our urban craftsmen have perfected the art of Filigran, intricate silver wirework that has become the hallmark of Bosnian luxury. These guilds operate as a powerful economic estate, exporting ceremonial daggers and fine jewelry to the markets of Venice and Vienna. By turning our raw mineral wealth into high-value artistic exports, we have created a prosperous urban middle class that is fiercely loyal to the Crown. This industrial refinement elevates the prestige of our nation in every foreign court, proving that the 'Iron Heart' of the Balkans possesses a sophisticated cultural edge that rivals the great capitals of the West.
expansive_policies: Brandenburg's infertile, sandy soil has earned it the unflattering nickname 'Sandbox of the Holy Roman Empire.' Such poverty spurred the margraves to aggressively expand, pursuing claims to neighboring territories. These conquests have made our country much more culturally diverse than the rest of the Empire.
northern_march: In the early days of the Holy Roman Empire, the Brandenburg area was settled and governed by Slavic tribes, until the Emperor created the Northern March to subjugate and fortify the area. Over time, this Northern March evolved into Brandenburg, becoming one of the most important regions in the Holy Roman Empire.
divide_estates: United, the three estates form an effective block against the power of the ruler. To consolidate our control, we must systematically leverage the nobility against the other estates.
soldiers_fortune: Our lands are sparsely populated, for the most part, and surrounded by enemies. The necessity for more robust defenses has prompted us to hire soldiers from foreign lands, who will fight under our banner for a price.
iron_tooth: Enhancing our court's control over the Margraviate's lands will earn our ruler the moniker Iron Tooth, as if we bit it like an attack dog. Our rule will leave a mark on our nation, a mark which will instill a sense of pride and loyalty in even the lowliest peasant in Brandenburg.
kammergericht: In order to regularize control of the Mark of Brandenburg, we will replace local common law with Roman law. We will further regulate justice by moving the Supreme Court from the court of the Elector, who is prone to moving around, to a fixed central location. This will simultaneously improve justice and curb the power of local magnates.
dispositio_achillea: Dividing our lands between heirs has weakened dynasties across the Empire. We will establish a clear rule of succession, the eldest inherits all. Our nobles may grumble, but an undivided Mark is worth their discontent.
margrave_council: The authority of the Margrave is greatly threatened by the ever-increasing power of our Estates. The Estates are of great benefit to our nation, but the threat they represent to our base of power necessitates the creation of a new council, one which reduces the very real power that the estates hold over our nation into more of an advisory position for the Margrave. This way, we may continue to enjoy the benefits of our Estates while having fewer concerns about their needs.
religious_toleration: Stability in our home regions is the key to our success elsewhere. Expanding outwards while fostering religious tolerance, we not only improve stability at home, but we also make our realm a haven for those fleeing persecution elsewhere.
hohenzollern_privy_council: Our estates have long held sway over the governance of the Mark. By establishing a council of advisors answerable to the Elector alone, we bring our ablest men to the center of power, and quietly reduce the estates to a consultative role.
edict_of_potsdam: Our neighbors drive out their most industrious subjects for the sake of religious conformity. Their loss is our gain. We open our doors to the persecuted and the skilled alike, and our cities grow richer for it.
hohenzollern_court_culture: A great court needs more than soldiers and clerks. By welcoming artists, philosophers, and men of science into our service, we turn the court of Brandenburg into a beacon of culture, and show the world that our ambitions reach beyond the battlefield.
berliner_aufklarung: New ideas spread fast in our cities, and the minds of Brandenburg have never been idle. We will cultivate this spirit of inquiry, drawing scholars and thinkers to our court. A nation that thinks clearly governs itself well.
breton_tradition: Ever since our ancestors came from Britain, our extensive coastal holdings have been bustling with activity. Our people live by the sea and for the sea, and our ports are always full of trade and fishing boats.
legacy_of_breton_independence: Brittany has never truly been part of France Though we have been ravaged by Franks, Vikings, and the English in the past, we have, thus far, maintained our unique identity as a people. Let all of our neighbors be aware that Brittany shall remain forever free, the last bastion of true Gallic traditions!
estates_of_brittany: First called in the 14th century, the Estates of Brittany allowed free men from all rungs of society, even the Third Estate, to share their grievances and petition the ruler for redress. By calling in the Estates, we can mitigate some of the tension felt throughout our domain.
byz_heart_of_orthodoxy_advance: Constantinople is the beating heart of vibrant faith. We take great pride in being the home of Orthodoxy, holders of the Ecumenical Patriarchate, and defenders of Christendom against our heathen enemies.
byz_cataphracts_advance: Although warfare has evolved significantly since the first incarnation of our empire, including the introduction of gunpowder, the battle tactics refined by our forebears centuries ago are often still effective. Our cataphracts shall embody the best of both our ancient and modern combat wisdom.
byz_akritai_advance: Primarily focused on border defense, these light troops are also given lands to farm as well as protect. Akritai are most adept at defensive warfare, especially against cavalry, and are often the first response against external threats.
byz_historiography_advance: Our people stand on the shoulders of giants; it is our responsibility to leave comprehensive records of our empire's glory to inspire and instruct future generations. By thoroughly documenting the lives of our extraordinary ancestors, tracing our prestigious lineages, and detailing our intricate traditions, we will surpass mere historical records and become truly legendary.
byz_bureaucracy_advance: Our administration heaves under the weight of our complex web of bureaucracies, a legacy of centuries of imperial rule.
men_of_letters_advance: It is no secret that other nations envy our literary accomplishments and enlightened past. They seek to hire tutors from our court, eager to sink their claws into the knowledge that gave rise to powerful empires and carved the cultural landscape of the entire continent. It is through these men of letters that our neighbors will come to fall in love with our history and become educated in our ways.
byz_shield_of_the_west: We stand between Europe and a sea of heathens, a shield against foreign threats. Our sword will forever be raised against those who seek to eradicate our faith, ready to strike against any who disrespect our traditions.
byz_court_of_languages: The court of Constantinople attracts diplomats and dignitaries from every corner of the known world. As a result, we ensure all languages receive equal respect and accommodation, a practical necessity for an empire at the crossroads of civilizations.
byz_poikilia: Byzantine culture has taken Europe by storm, particularly poikilia, our unique aesthetic. Emphasizing visual variety and a dizzying array of vibrant hues, poikilia creates a symphony of colors and elements in our art and architecture alike.
expand_varangian_guard_advance: The Varangians have served our country for centuries with distinguished honor and unwavering faith. By expanding their ranks, we will further secure the stability and protection of Byzantium.
byz_crossroads_of_continents: Byzantium is located between Europe and Asia, making it in many ways the connection between East and West. Our advantageous position is highly lucrative, and has also allowed us to significantly expand our maritime influence.
byz_the_new_helepolis: We are already familiar with deploying and refining powerful siege engines. However, by adapting our designs to use gunpowder, we will be able to completely dominate our foes with our cannons.
byz_reaffirm_synod_powers: Bureaucracy is a nightmarish endeavor for a country our size. To better refine the religious proceedings required every time we call the Orthodox Synod, we will cut down on the red tape, and revisit the associated legislation.
byz_byzantine_inquisition: Europe is engulfed in religious turmoil. We must be prepared to rip up noxious weeds of heresy that appear in the garden of our Empire, lest it become overgrown with heathens. Our pious defense against heretic incursion will prevent us from sinking into instability.
byz_autokratoria_rhomaion: Our great nation is the undisputed heir to the splendor and prestige of Rome, and reclaiming that long-lost territory is our primary motivation.
byz_modernized_strategikon: The Strategikon (the ancient manual of cavalry tactics, logistics, and battlefield doctrine) has served us well in times of war. However, as war changes, so must we. Our tactics and regiments have adapted to modern combat, employing weapons of such destruction that Maurice himself could never have anticipated their devastation.
byz_ancient_greek_studies: The rediscovery and revival of ancient Greek arts has provided us with a wonderful opportunity to better educate the masses and to preserve our lofty scientific and cultural ideals. We shall make a diligent study of the wisdom of our ancestors.
byz_the_new_imperial_army: Our army has lagged behind others in Europe for far too long. By enacting sweeping military reform and expanding our conscription efforts, we hope to build a modern army befitting the resurgent and resplendent phoenix that symbolizes our empire.
cas_repoblaciones: The Repoblación is our standing policy of resettling territories reconquered from Moorish rule, granting fueros and tax exemptions to draw colonists southward. Under kings like Alfonso VI and Ferdinand III, vast tracts of Toledo, La Mancha, and Andalusia have been claimed by frontier councils of free settlers who hold their lands directly from the Crown. This systematic colonization turns conquest into permanence, fixing Castilian populations on every frontier and preventing the territorial reversal that ended earlier reconquest waves.
cas_a_land_of_castles: Castile takes its very name from the network of castillos (castles, fortresses, and watchtowers) that has crowned every defensible ridge along the Duero, the Tagus, and the Guadiana since the ninth-century repopulation of the Meseta. Strongholds like Burgos, Gormaz, Calatrava, and the dozens of keeps of the Castillos de la Frontera are raised, manned, and maintained by frontier councils (concejos) and the military orders of Santiago and Calatrava under royal charter. Centuries of building have given our Crown a chain of strongholds along every frontier.
cas_camino_de_santiago: The Camino de Santiago threads west across our realm from the Pyrenees through Burgos, Carrión, and León toward Compostela, carrying a ceaseless stream of pilgrims, friars, and foreign merchants along its hospices and bridges. The towns strung along the road grow fat on the pilgrim trade, their fueros drawing settlers to repopulate the meseta in the road's wake. This great artery of devotion and commerce fills our frontier towns with people and binds the Christian north into a single road of faith.
crd_city_of_the_caliphs: From 929 the Umayyad Ḵilāfa made Madīnat Qurṭuba the largest and most learned city of the Latin and Islamic West, its streets paved and lamplit, its great mosque and the palace city of Madīnat az-Zahrā the wonders of the age. Though Ferdinand III restored it to Christian rule in 1236, the memory of that splendor still clings to every quarter and lends its archbishopric and lords an outsized weight. We trade on the renown of a capital whose name once carried from Baghdad to Aachen, drawing scholars, pilgrims, and embassies far beyond what our present strength could command.
jae_llave_de_castilla: Jaén bears upon its arms the legend Guarda y Defendimiento de los Reinos de Castilla, guard and defense of the Castilian realms, earned by two centuries holding the front line against Nasrid Granada. Its ring of frontier castillos, from Santa Catalina above the city to the watchtowers strung along the sierra, channels every raid and counter-raid across the border. This fortified frontier role makes the kingdom Castile's shield in the south and breeds a population hardened to constant war.
muc_huerta_acequias: The Huerta de Murcia is watered by a dense web of acequias, gravity canals laid out by Andalusi engineers and still governed by the ancient Consejo de Hombres Buenos water court that settles every dispute over a share of the Segura. Our gardeners raise mulberry, citrus, and vegetables in such abundance that land which without the river would be steppe yields several harvests a year. This irrigation network makes the Murcian plain one of the most intensively productive landscapes in all Iberia.
sev_guadalquivir_port: Seville sits at the head of navigation on the Guadalquivir, the only great river port of Iberia where ocean-going ships ride the tide fifty miles inland to moor beneath the city walls. Our quays load the oil and wine of the Aljarafe and the wool of the interior, and unload the fish, cloth, and timber of the wider sea. This inland deep-water harbor makes Seville the natural emporium of the south and the meeting point of river and ocean trade.
tol_primate_see: The Archbishop of Toledo is Primado de las Españas, the senior prelate of the peninsula by right of the Visigothic councils that met in the city before 711. Our see commands the wealthiest diocese in Spain, a vast network of suffragan bishoprics, and a voice no king can safely ignore in matters of Church and Crown alike. Our primacy in the Church brings the kingdom great religious authority and a steady stream of tithe and patronage.
cas_castilian_navy: With our peninsular coastline divided between the rough Cantabrian Sea and the Atlantic approaches, our navy has long been a pillar of state survival, commanded by the office of Almirante Mayor de Castilla. From Santander to Sevilla, our shipyards have fielded fleets that outmatched English and Hanseatic squadrons throughout the late medieval Cantabrian wars, and admirals like Pero Niño have raided as far as the Thames. This navy is ready for the deep waters that the coming age of oceanic empire will demand.
cas_cronicas_reales: In the tradition of Alfonso X the Wise's Estoria de España, the royal chancery has long commissioned official chronicles of each reign, such as the Crónica de Alfonso XI, Pedro López de Ayala's accounts of the Trastámara civil wars, and Hernando del Pulgar's Crónica de los Reyes Católicos. By compiling these into a single dynastic history, we anchor every Castilian king to a continuous Visigothic and Reconquista lineage stretching back to Pelayo of Asturias. Written this way, our dynasty's legitimacy stretches unbroken back to Pelayo.
cas_santa_hermandad: The hermandades, sworn brotherhoods of the Castilian towns, band their militias together to police the roads, hunt down bandits, and keep the king's peace where the crown's own officers cannot reach. Armed with crossbow and pike and answerable to their own elected alcaldes, these leagues field a standing rural constabulary that overawes unruly nobles and footpads alike. Funded by its own members, the brotherhood keeps order in the realm without burdening the royal treasury.
crd_silver_filigree: The metalworkers of Córdoba inherit the Andalusi mastery of filigrana, silver and gold drawn into wire so fine it is worked into lace-like ornament, reliquaries, and jewelry without equal in the north. From the silversmiths' quarter beside the old mosque, our craftsmen supply the luxury markets of Castile, Genoa, and the Maghreb with goods that command high prices wherever they are sold. This concentration of fine artisanship fixes skilled hands and their wealth in the city and burnishes its reputation as a center of craft.
jae_olive_presses: The rolling country of Jaén is one unbroken mar de olivos, a sea of olive groves that since Roman Baetica has clothed every hill in silver-grey. Our almazaras press the autumn harvest into oil stored in great earthenware tinajas and carried by mule train to markets across the peninsula and beyond. This olive monoculture makes the province the foremost oil producer of the south and the engine of its rural wealth.
muc_silk_looms: The mulberry groves of the huerta feed a flourishing sericultura, and the looms of the city and its morerías weave the reeled silk into taffetas and velvets prized across the kingdom. This silk rearing and weaving, inherited from al-'Andalus, occupies a great part of the city's households from the spring hatching of the worms to the winter sale of the cloth. This silk industry is the signature manufacture of the Murcian realm and the foundation of its urban wealth.
sev_merchant_fairs: Seville's fairs and its resident colonies of Genoese, Florentine, and Burgalese factors make the city the busiest marketplace of the peninsula well before the age of the Indies. Our exchange handles bills, marine insurance, and cargoes for merchants from across the Mediterranean and the Atlantic, lending the city a commercial sophistication few rivals possess. This established merchant community lays the financial foundation on which the city's coming greatness will be built.
tol_school_of_translators: From the twelfth century the Escuela de Traductores de Toledo gathers Christian, Jewish, and Muslim scholars under archiepiscopal and later royal patronage to render the science and philosophy of the Arabic world into Latin and Castilian. Gerard of Cremona, Michael Scot, and the teams of Alfonso X recover Aristotle, Ptolemy, Euclid, and the medicine of Avicenna for all of Christendom. This work of translation makes Toledo the great intellectual gateway between the Islamic and Latin worlds and a magnet for learned men.
cas_masters_of_the_orders: With the Reconquista complete, the three great Castilian military orders (Santiago, Calatrava, and Alcántara) possess vast estates and private armies but no remaining enemies to fight. The Catholic Monarchs have begun a quiet annexation, by which the Crown will assume the Grand Mastership of each order, transferring their lands, encomiendas, and bullion under royal control. This absorption eliminates the last great rivals to royal power within Castile and adds an unmatched military and religious strength to the permanent resources of the Crown.
cas_audiencias: The royal Audiencias and Chancillerías, the high courts seated at Valladolid and later Granada, carry the king's justice into every corner of the realm, hearing appeals that once died in the courts of grasping lords. Their robed oidores, trained in Roman law at Salamanca, bind noble and commoner alike to a single royal jurisdiction. This apparatus of crown justice knits the kingdom together and strips the great houses of the legal independence that breeds revolt.
cas_new_world: Columbus's landfall and the Capitulations of Santa Fe have placed the lands and peoples beyond the Ocean Sea under the Crown of Castile. We will charter conquistadors and licensed colonists on the encomienda pattern, granting them rights over indigenous labor in exchange for evangelization and a fifth, the quinto real, of all metals struck from the new soil. Castile alone, of all European powers, holds a system of rule already prepared to absorb a hemisphere.
crd_cordwainer_guilds: Córdoba lent its name to cordobán, the supple goatskin leather, and the gilded and painted guadamecí wall hangings, whose tanning and tooling its guilds have perfected since the caliphate. Our curtidores and guadamecileros along the Guadalquivir supply shoes, bookbindings, harness, and leathers prized in every court of Europe. This signature craft anchors a steady export trade and a guild structure that organizes a great share of the city's working hands.
jae_linares_lead: The district of Linares and the Sierra Morena have yielded lead and silver-bearing galena since the mines of Cástulo supplied Carthage and Rome. Our smelters cast the pig lead that lines hulls and roofs and the shot that fills the kingdom's powder magazines. Jaén now has mineral wealth wholly distinct from its olive groves and a workforce of hardened miners.
muc_consulado_de_la_seda: Murcia secures a royal charter for a Consulado de la Seda: a silk exchange and merchant guild empowered to inspect quality, settle commercial suits, and finance the shipment of cloth through the ports of Cartagena and Alicante. Our merchants gain a recognized corporation to represent them before the Crown and foreign buyers, with its own jurisdiction and reserve funds. This institution turns a scattered cottage trade into an organized and far-reaching commercial engine.
sev_casa_de_contratacion: The Crown establishes the Casa de Contratación at Seville to license, register, and tax every ship, passenger, and cargo bound for the Indies, and to keep in its Padrón Real the master chart of the new ocean. Our city becomes the sole legal gateway of the New World trade, its pilots examined and its homecoming bullion weighed under royal officials. This monopoly draws the silver of two continents through a single river port and makes Seville the richest and most coveted city in Europe.
tol_toledan_steel: The swordsmiths of Toledo forge blades of a temper renowned across Europe since antiquity, their secret lying in fine sand-quenched steel cooled in the waters of the Tagus and in the jealously guarded craft of the guild. Our espaderos, each stamping his own mark on the blade, arm the finest soldiers of the age and export swords to courts as distant as Italy and the Indies. This steelcraft makes the city's name a byword for the highest quality of arms.
cas_marine_infantry: Emperor Charles V created the Compañías Viejas del Mar de Nápoles, the world's first standing marine infantry corps, raised to crew the tercios serving aboard the galleys of the Mediterranean. These Infantes de Marina are trained for the close quarters chaos of boarding actions and for garrisoning fortified coastal outposts from Oran to Manila. This permanent assault arm multiplies the value of every flagship and secures the coastal links of an empire stretching across two oceans.
cas_armada_real: The Armada Real musters the galleons and galleys of Cantabria, Andalusia, and Naples into a single royal fleet that escorts the treasure convoys and contests the seas from the Channel to the Levant. Our dockyards at Santander and the arsenals of the south build and refit the great ships, while a corps of trained crews man them through every campaign. A standing royal navy carries the historical Crown's reach across the open ocean, beyond anything a breakaway successor could assemble.
cas_reform_of_millones: The Servicio de Millones, first authorized by the Cortes of Castile after the disaster of the Armada, is an indirect excise on the four staples (wine, oil, vinegar, and meat) sold in the kingdom. Renewed every six years under negotiated terms with the eighteen voting cities, it bypasses noble and clerical tax exemptions by being levied on consumption rather than property ownership. This single reform nearly doubles ordinary Crown revenue at the moment of greatest fiscal strain, ideally sustaining the Habsburg war machine into the next century.
crd_andalusi_libraries: The caliphal library of al-Ḥakam II was said to hold four hundred thousand volumes when the rest of Europe counted its books in dozens, and the recovered remnants of that learning seed the schools of our restored city. Scholars gather to copy, translate, and teach the mathematics, medicine, and philosophy that Córdoba preserved through the dark centuries. This depth of inherited learning draws talent from across the peninsula and raises the literacy and standing of our clergy and jurists.
jae_frontier_jinetes: Generations facing Granada have bred a class of jinetes, light horsemen riding a la jineta with short stirrups, leather adarga shield, and a brace of javelins, a style learned from the Moorish enemy himself. Our riders raid, ambush, and screen with a speed and endurance the heavy lance knights of the north cannot match. Our armies gain a swift, seasoned, and inexpensive mounted arm, ideally suited to border war.
muc_baroque_processions: The Holy Week of Murcia grows into one of the great devotional spectacles of the south, its cofradías parading sculpted pasos of the Passion through streets packed with the faithful. The brotherhoods vie to commission ever more vivid polychrome figures, binding nobles, guildsmen, and laborers alike into a shared liturgical theater. This processional culture cements civic identity and popular piety in a form that Crown and Church alike can celebrate and steer.
sev_triana_ceramics: Across the river in Triana, generations of potters fire the tin-glazed azulejos and earthenware that tile the floors, façades, and altars of the kingdom and its colonies. Our kilns turn out both the geometric Mudéjar patterns inherited from al-'Andalus and the new figurative panels demanded by churches and palaces. This ceramic craft is a distinctive and lucrative trade that ships its wares the length of the peninsula and across the Atlantic.
tol_imperial_cortes: As the old Visigothic and imperial capital, sometime seat of Charles V himself, Toledo is a favored place for the solemn Cortes of the realm, where kings, prelates, grandees, and the procurators of the cities convene. Our chambers host the great assemblies that vote on the extraordinary taxes, settle the succession, and swear in the heir. This role as a seat of the Cortes places the kingdom at the ceremonial and political center of royal governance.
cas_pasos: The Pasos of Holy Week (massive sculpted scenes of the Passion carried in procession through our streets) have become the defining popular art of the Castilian Baroque. Sculptors such as Juan de Juni in Valladolid and Gregorio Fernández, working in polychrome wood, have raised the form to its peak in the early seventeenth century, producing figures so anatomically vivid that crowds weep at their passage. This processional culture binds the urban populace, the parish brotherhoods, and the Crown in a shared devotional spectacle that no Protestant nation can match.
cas_consejo_de_castilla: The Consejo de Castilla sits at the apex of the realm's government, a council of letrados that drafts the laws, supervises the courts and the treasury, and governs in the king's name when he is abroad or at war. Its committees and corregidores reach down into every city and province, turning royal will into administrative fact. Through the council the Crown governs with a reach and continuity that no other institution of the realm can equal.
cas_real_academia_espanola: Founded by Juan Manuel Fernández Pacheco, Marquis of Villena, on the model of the Académie française, the Real Academia Española takes as its motto Limpia, fija y da esplendor (to clean, fix, and give splendor to the Castilian tongue). Its first great project, the six-volume Diccionario de Autoridades, sets the standards of orthography, grammar, and usage that will bind together every Castilian writer from Cádiz to Lima. This institution makes our language the most regulated and exportable of the great European vernaculars, an instrument of empire as much as of letters.
crd_andalusian_horse: The river meadows of the Guadalquivir breed the caballo andaluz: the Córdoba warhorse whose compact power, high gait, and steadiness under arms make it the most prized mount in Europe. Our stud farms, later formalized in the royal Caballerizas, refine a bloodline sought by every court and cavalry of the age. Our breeding supplies the kingdom with a valuable export and with superb light horses for its own squadrons.
jae_royal_mines: The Crown brings the silver and lead districts of the Sierra Morena under direct administration as minas reales, appointing salaried overseers, guaranteeing timber and labor, and reserving the richest seams to the treasury. The bullion and lead of the south flow straight into royal coffers rather than dissipating among private adventurers. This crown control over the mines turns them into a dependable and rising pillar of state finance.
muc_cartagena_arsenal: The deep natural harbor of Cartagena, sheltered behind its ring of hills, is fortified and fitted out as a royal naval arsenal with dry docks, rope walks, foundries, and shipways for the Mediterranean fleet. Our base builds, repairs, and victuals the squadrons that guard the Levantine coast and the convoys bound for Italy. This arsenal makes the Murcian realm an indispensable pillar of the monarchy's sea power in the western Mediterranean.
sev_jabon_works: The jabón de Sevilla (hard white soap boiled from the olive oil of the Aljarafe and the ash of coastal barrilla) is produced under royal license in the great almonas of Triana, a monopoly dating to the Reconquista. Our soap houses supply a staple demanded in every household of the kingdom and shipped in quantity to the Indies. This manufacture converts the region's abundant oil into a durable and profitable export.
tol_royal_armory: The bladesmiths of Toledo, long organized in their guild, are gathered by the Crown into a Real Fábrica de Armas charged with arming the royal infantry to a single tested standard. Our armory turns out swords and, as the age demands, bayonets and firearms, its proof marks guaranteeing every weapon issued. This royal manufacture binds the city's ancient craft directly to the military needs of the state.
cas_canal_de_castilla: Begun under the patronage of the Marquis of Ensenada, the Canal de Castilla cuts north from the Tierra de Campos through Palencia and Valladolid toward the Cantabrian ports. Its locks, aqueducts, and bridges allow the wheat surplus of the Meseta to reach Santander cheaply enough to compete with Baltic grain on European markets. This single feat of engineering transforms Old Castile from a landlocked breadbasket trapped behind the Cordillera into the granary of the Atlantic seaboard.
cas_royal_arsenals: The royal arsenals and Reales Fábricas de Armas gather the realm's gunsmiths and founders into crown manufactories that arm the regiments to a single proofed standard. Cannon from the foundries, muskets from the workshops, and powder from the royal mills flow to the garrisons through a state-run ordnance system. This military-industrial backbone keeps the historical Crown's armies equipped at a scale and consistency that no successor state could improvise.
cas_royal_factories: To break the dependence on foreign manufactures that drains American silver from the kingdom, the Bourbon kings are founding Reales Fábricas, state-owned manufactories producing luxury goods according to mercantilist principles. The Real Fábrica de Tapices of Madrid, the Real Fábrica de Cristales at La Granja, and the woolen manufactories of Guadalajara employ thousands under royal protection, with foreign masters imported to teach Flemish, Bohemian, and English techniques. This industrial program reverses the eighteenth-century trade deficit and seeds the manufacturing base from which a later industrial revolution can emerge.
crd_sierra_morena_mining: The wooded ridges of the Sierra Morena north of the city hold copper, lead, and coal worked since Roman Corduba, now reopened by chartered companies and foreign capital. Mining settlements, smelters, and the roads to serve them rise across hills that for centuries held only pasture and bandits. Mineral wealth turns the old caliphal capital into a modern industrial center, with a source of revenue beyond its fields and crafts.
jae_mining_boomtowns: Drawn by foreign capital and the new steam pumps that drain the deep shafts, Linares and La Carolina swell from frontier villages into crowded mining towns ringed by headframes and smelters. Tens of thousands of miners, engineers, and their families pour into hills that a century before held only olive pickers and bandits. This mining boom turns the old Granadan frontier into one of the most populous and productive districts of the south.
muc_la_union_mining: The hills of the Sierra de Cartagena around La Unión are honeycombed with shafts for lead, silver, and zinc, drawing tens of thousands into a frenzied nineteenth-century rush worked by hand and steam alike. Our smelters and the quays of Cartagena ship the refined metal across the Mediterranean and beyond. The mineral boom pours immense new wealth into the kingdom and fills the southern coast with a teeming industrial workforce.
sev_trade_emporium: Seville stands as the commercial capital of the south, its riverside Lonja and the counting houses of its merchants commanding the trade of the whole Guadalquivir basin and the Andalusian hinterland. Our markets gather the oil, wine, cloth, and metals of the region for sale and shipment along the river and out to sea.
