ser_serbian_national_militia: Drawing from the hard-won experience of our veteran units of the previous decades, we have established a permanent, professional standing National Militia. This force represents a decisive move away from the disorganized peasant levy, utilizing rigorous Western drill, uniform equipment, and a modernized chain of command while retaining the fierce, high-morale fighting style of our Balkan predecessors. This ensures that our independence is not a fragile diplomatic gift, but is instead backed by a credible, modern military machine that can defend our borders against any encroaching imperial power.
foreign_relations_bureau: Our realm has recognized the importance of fostering friendly relations and alliances with neighboring countries. To facilitate this, we will establish a specialized bureau dedicated to foreign affairs. By maintaining a dedicated focus on diplomacy, we are better positioned to navigate the complex web of international relations and secure our nation's prosperity.
tro_the_zudiosca_network: As the great Mediterranean wars intensify, the Travunjan state will draw upon its unique relationship with the Jewish and Ragusan merchant families (the Zudiosca) to build a sophisticated espionage ring. Because these traders move freely between the mountain interior and the Adriatic ports, they provide the Travunjan commanders with real-time troop movements of foreign armies. This 'Invisible Guard' will allow the local army to always strike at the enemy's weakest point, effectively nullifying the numbers of any invading power.
zta_guerillas_of_the_scrub: The Gola Brda (Naked Hills) of the karst offer absolutely no cover for a traditional invading army, but they provide infinite hideouts and ambush points for our nimble warriors. We have developed a sophisticated tactical doctrine of 'Night-Raiding', where our clansmen descend silently from the peaks under the total cover of darkness to butcher enemy camps, spike their cannons, and vanish back into the mist before the first light of dawn. This psychological warfare ensures that any occupying force in the lowlands is driven to the brink of madness by constant fear and physical exhaustion, making our territory a nightmare they eventually choose to abandon, while adapting our armies to any hostile territory.
serbian_enlightenment: Inspired by other nations of the Enlightenment, our national heroes, such as Dositej Obradović, have sought to elevate our vernacular language and literature. Touched by the dearth of secular works accessible to the common folk, Dositej Obradović has taken the lead in bridging the gap between written and spoken Shtokavian. By diligently crafting grammar books and dictionaries, authoring new tomes, and translating foreign works, our nation is fostering a literary revival thanks to the work of these visionaries.
hum_modernized_national_redoubt: Refining centuries of mountain warfare, we have implemented the 'National Redoubt' doctrine, where every major city and pass is integrated into a single, cohesive defensive plan. Using modern Western ballistics and cartography, we have pre-positioned batteries and supplies in hidden mountain caches. This doctrine ensures that even if the valleys are lost, the state can continue to function as a sovereign military entity from the high peaks, mocking any occupier with a permanent, active resistance that makes the cost of holding Hum prohibitively expensive for any empire.
military_modernization: Our people remember the birth of our nation: surrounded by formidable powers that pose permanent, looming threats to our security. This enduring vigilance has forged a culture of unwavering readiness, ensuring our armed forces stand as a shield against adversity. Fearless and respected, our soldiers have transformed us from potential prey to a mighty adversary, deterring any who dare encroach upon our sovereignty.
ser_the_sumadija_agrarian_revolution: The Serbian peasantry has led its own cultural and economic revolution by adopting agrarian techniques learned from the West. This has turned the dense forests of Šumadija into a highly productive agricultural heartland. This surplus of food does not just feed the people; it fuels a demographic explosion. A well-fed Serbian population is a growing and ambitious one, providing a massive pool of young, healthy recruits for the army and a robust internal market that makes Serbia the dominant economic engine of the Central Balkans.
tro_the_constitution_of_trebinje: The state will introduce a written constitution that will limit the power of the ruler and grant rights to the 'Assembly of Lords and Citizens'. This will be one of the first liberal documents in the Balkans, intended to prevent internal revolution and present Travunja as a 'Civilized State' to the great powers of Europe, ensuring our continued sovereignty.
zta_the_code_of_the_black_mountain: To finally transition from a loose tribal federation to a modern, centralized state, we have introduced a rigorous and uncompromising new legal code that strictly suppresses the destructive tradition of blood feuds and centralizes the power of the Vladika. By replacing ancient tribal law with a uniform system of state justice and taxation, we unify the competing clans into a single, cohesive national body. This reform turns the disparate and often chaotic energy of the mountains into a focused, disciplined national force capable of reclaiming our ancestral coastlines and expanding our borders with the efficiency of a modern European power.
sia_experienced_ambassadors: We have extensive political experience. The birth of our country was something achieved not only with the power of our military, after all. Surely our diplomatic reputation will prove to be a source of our influence on the world stage.
sia_rise_to_equal_heights: There are many parts of our country with very low population. We should improve conditions in these regions to ensure that no part of our country is seen as lackluster, and all of it shines equally.
sia_advanced_elephant_warfare: It is not uncommon for our greatest poems to dedicate lines of text to list and honor our war elephants individually. Let us show our enemies why!
sia_consolidation_of_state: A decentralized system may cause us to lose control over our more distant provinces. If we are to be the true unifying realm for the Thai people, our provinces must be unified as well.
sia_education_reform: As our Lord Buddha said, we shall not accept something because it is often said, but we need to experience it ourselves. Education is the basis of knowledge, and if we want to excel at technology, we need to excel at education first.
sia_royal_absolutism: Second only to Heaven — that is what a ruler should be. Honored and worshipped, our leaders rule over the Earth as the Gods rule over Heaven.
sia_thai_unity: We are undoubtedly the leaders of all Thai people. Our troops are proud to serve as defenders of our culture and identity itself, and they fight fiercely for the privilege.
sme_jaqeli_dynasty: Despite its humble origins, the Jaqeli dynasty has been able to establish many successful relationships, forging strong ties to the rulers of surrounding states. As such, we have a positive reputation in the diplomatic sphere.
sme_atabegs_of_samtskhe: We are not just one part of the Kingdom of Georgia, as a long time ago we received royal recognition and, with it, the title of Atabeg. This title had previously been granted only to the Armenian vassals, and therefore its conveyance is a sign of distinction and of the respect that the Georgian monarch has for us.
sme_proactive_diplomacy: While still a part of Georgia, Samtskhe operates with substantial independence. This privileged position requires constant diplomatic awareness and a policy of active diplomacy, ensuring that we always have a direct channel to those in power. We do all this while actively engaging in our internal politics, meddling with the succession and forging dynastic alliances as best benefits us. The survival of our relatively small state depends on upholding these diplomatic traditions. Let it never be said that we have done too little or acted without sufficient wisdom!
sme_fortresses_of_samtskhe: Our mountainous terrain has acted as a shield against foreign invaders many times. Because of this, we learned to build strong fortresses and to always be prepared for defensive warfare. This legacy of strength and readiness is one we must strive at all costs to uphold — the fortresses of Samtskhe must be perpetually well maintained, manned, and supplied, as foreign invaders are not a possibility but a certainty.
sme_independent_ambitions: Samtskhe has often been obligated to bow to foreign rulers, be they Muslim or Christian; Georgian, Turkic, or Iranian. To build an enduring state that survives as an independent entity and can stand against covetous outsiders, we must establish independent institutions: issuing our own coinage, creating our own laws, and patronizing our own theologians and writers.
sme_protect_trade_routes: Our position at the crossroads of Georgia, Anatolia, Armenia, and Āzarbāijān also means that a great number of traders seek to cross our lands. However, the constant threat of being raided by nomadic tribesmen means that some have come to doubt the safety of traveling on our roads. We must properly defend all roads and merchant inns in our nation so that trade revenue can flow into our state treasury unhindered.
sme_frontier_warriors: The Caucasus have been shaped by nomadic emperors since time immemorial, but the lush pastures of Samtskhe have convinced many tribesmen to settle. We must not let this affect the stability of our kingdom, but instead make arrangements with these settling tribes so that they contribute to our military ambitions in exchange for the lands they claim.
sme_sacred_land: The lands of Samtskhe are home to places both sacred and revered among the Georgian people. The cave monastery of Vardzia, the ancient church of Atskuri with its miraculous icon of the Virgin Mary, and the Monastery of Ancha with its Anchiskhati icon, are some of the most significant holy places in our realm. By protecting and curating the Samtskhe church, setting it apart as distinct from that of Georgia, we ensure that our people stand united even in the face of adversity.
sme_bridge_between_worlds: Our country has always served as a bridge between the Christian and Muslim worlds. As such, people of both faiths within our borders have become accustomed to interacting with each other.
stories_of_the_gao_empire: Before the Malian Empire came to dominate Western Africa, the city of Gao was the capital of an empire in its own right. Although there are barely any written records of the Gao Empire, its legacy lives on in our oral traditions, inspiring all who want to achieve greatness one day.
malian_military_tactics: During our time as subjects of Mali, our people learned much from their military command and combat tactics. This knowledge shall help our own infantry in battles to come.
gold_to_salt_trade: Some say that Salt is worth its weight in Gold... perhaps it would be more accurate to say that Gold is worth its weight in Salt. Either way, by exchanging these two commodities, we have established thriving trade networks.
independence_from_mali: For many years, we were a subject of Mali. As Mali's power has weakened, ours has grown, and we can now claim to be fully independent of Malian overlordship. Let us take steps to make sure we remain so.
jihad_against_the_pagans: Despite the best efforts of centuries of Sunni sultanates, Western Africa is still plagued by the menace of Animistic pagans. By lifting the banner of Jihād, we can cleanse our lands of the unbelievers and expand our frontiers at the same time.
sankore_madrassah: We have been told that the Sankoré Mosque's school is the greatest center for learning in the entirety of Africa. Who could be surprised if this were true, given how many wise men from distant Arabia and the Maghreb are here right now, arguing the finer points of philosophy and religion?
the_hajj: Like Mansa Mūsā of Mali once did, our rulers can travel to Mecca on pilgrimage, fulfilling the fifth pillar of Islam and bearing gold as a symbol of our wealth and power. Like the Malian pilgrims of old, the world will gasp in wonder at the wealth and grandeur of Songhai.
sharia: The Holy Law that the Prophet followed when ruling Madīna should be the unshakable foundation of the laws we use to run our society. By reforming our criminal code to reflect the teachings of the Prophet, we will bring harmony and justice to our people.
trans_sahara_trade: Our traders frequently bring back fascinating things from the courts of North Africa. Perhaps they could find and bring back yet more fascinating trinkets?
modernization_of_the_military: Our state lives and dies by the capabilities of our army. Our military not only ensures our survival, but is also what has set us on the path to greatness. We cannot allow ourselves to fall behind in progress!
spa_visigothic_inheritance: The Christian kingdoms of Iberia claim continuity with the unified Visigothic monarchy that ruled Hispania from Toledo until the Muslim conquest of 711. Our chroniclers trace every king of León and Castile back through Pelayo to Reccared and the Toledan Crown, framing the Reconquista as a Restauratio, the restoration of one rightful Christian kingdom rather than the conquest of several. The Neo-Gothic ideology offers the Spanish Crown a unifying narrative that justifies a single peninsular monarchy stretching from the Pyrenees to the Strait of Gibraltar.
spa_idea_de_hispania: The chroniclers and jurists of the peninsular courts revive the Idea de Hispania, the Visigothic-Roman conception of Iberia as a single Christian community of crowns sharing one historical destiny and one legal inheritance. We will compile the genealogies, conciliar decrees, and crusading bulls that bind the peninsular monarchies into a recognizable political family, and our chanceries will adopt the formulas of Hispanic legitimacy that distinguish our kings from the merely regional dynasties beyond the Pyrenees. This shared ideal lets our chanceries draw on a common body of precedent to streamline our own lawmaking, while our place within this recognized Christian family of crowns means neighboring courts read our actions as those of a kindred realm rather than a threat.
spa_revival_of_ecclesiastical_discipline: The Spanish religious orders stand on the threshold of the Observancia, the movement for stricter monastic discipline, already taking root among the Franciscan and Dominican houses of Castile. We will extend Crown backing to the observant branches of every regular order, suppressing the conventual houses that have abandoned enclosure and redirecting their endowments toward the reformed Hieronymites, Augustinians, Carthusians, and Cistercians under joint Crown and inquisitorial visitation. A thoroughgoing reform of the regular clergy gives the Spanish Church a disciplined moral order a generation before the rest of Catholic Europe even faces the question.
spa_school_salamanca: The Escuela de Salamanca (the school of theologians and jurists centered on the Universidad de Salamanca through the sixteenth century) applies Thomist scholastic methods to the unprecedented questions of empire, conquest, and global commerce. Francisco de Vitoria's lectures on the rights of the Amerindians, Domingo de Soto's monetary theory, and Luis de Molina's treatment of free will produce the first systematic European thinking on natural law, international law, and economic theory. The school arms the Spanish monarchy with a body of ideas to justify its imperial project, a generation ahead of any rival power.
spa_siglo_de_oro: Spain stands at the cusp of an unprecedented cultural flowering, the Siglo de Oro whose first stirrings are already visible in Antonio de Nebrija's Castilian grammar and the artistic circles of the Catholic Monarchs' court. We will channel royal patronage toward poets, dramatists, and painters through the Real Casa and the chapters of the religious orders, providing the institutional support that Cervantes, Lope de Vega, Velázquez, and Calderón will require to produce their masterworks. This sustained cultural investment turns Spain into the literary and artistic capital of the Catholic world for two centuries.
spa_spanish_enlightenment: The Bourbon reform programs of Charles III and his ministers (Floridablanca, Aranda, and Campomanes) open Spain to the wider European Enlightenment in the second half of the eighteenth century. Gaspar Melchor de Jovellanos publishes his agrarian reports, the Reales Sociedades Económicas de Amigos del País spread across every provincial capital, and the universities of Salamanca, Alcalá, and Valencia introduce modern physics, chemistry, and political economy into their curricula; the Real Ordenanza de la Casa de la Moneda brings Newtonian assaying standards to every royal mint from Sevilla to Potosí; and the new Banco de San Carlos at Madrid pools merchant capital and Crown deposits to finance public projects at terms no private banker can offer. Intellectual and fiscal modernization equips the late Spanish monarchy with the trained ministers, administrative innovation, public credit at sovereign rates, and productive silver mint required to compete in the new continental order.
suk_breaker_of_chains: It was not so long ago that we saw ourselves under the Khmer authority, but we have since gained our freedom, and have taken our rightful place as an independent power. We have earned the admiration of our peers, and their respect.
suk_akson_sukhothai: Although the Thai script is already common to all Thai people, it should not be forgotten that it was in our country and under our guidance that it was developed. As such, Thai script is not only a unifying force for our culture, but also proof of our individuality and distinctiveness.
suk_birthplace_of_a_culture: We are called the first independent Thai kingdom, as we were the first ones to rebel against Khmer authority and establish ourselves as free from their influence. As such, all Thai people look at us in admiration.
suk_ram_khamhaeng_stele: Most of the history of the early Sukhothai kingdom comes from inscriptions on the Ram Khamhaeng Stele, commissioned by the great king to give a record of his glorious reign. The Ram Khamhaeng Stele is a sacred piece of heritage and one that surely proves our place in history.
suk_wat_si_sawai: We are known for our many gorgeous temples, such as the Wat Si Sawai, one of the oldest in Sukhothai. Built under the Khmer authority as a Hindu temple, its ensuing repurposing has turned it into a symbol of our identity. The faith of our people is strong.
suk_sukhothai_ceramics: Ceramics have been created by the Thai people since antiquity, influenced by Chinese ceramics but always retaining their own distinct style. However, the ceramics produced in our country are most valued, and they are often traded at great distances overseas.
suk_military_history: Our armies have a long history of victory in combat. As a result, a position in our military is seen as a post of honor and prestige, and there are many willing to serve.
suk_unstoppable_army: Many have tried in the past to stop our progress and expansion, but all have failed in the face of our army. It has proved to be an unstoppable force, one that readily crushes any obstacles in our way.
seren_taun: Held after the harvest, the Sérén Taun festival is an annual thanksgiving ceremony celebrating agricultural abundance. Marked by rituals, offerings, and music, it strengthens the communal bonds of our kampung-kampung and reminds all of the sacred balance between people, rice, and nature.
pepper_of_the_parahyangan: The fertile volcanic soil of the Sundanese highlands is perfect for growing the prized spice, black pepper. Traders from across the world seek our peppercorns for their potency and aroma. We must capitalize on this natural treasure to expand our influence through spice.
pan_asian_trade: Sunda lies at the crossroads of great empires: India, China, and the Islamic world. By positioning ourselves as an indispensable node in this network, we secure access to goods, ideas, and partners across Asia turning our harbors into gateways of prosperity.
extend_kampung_kampung: The foundation of Sundanese society lies in every kampung, rural communities that dot the landscape. Investing in the infrastructure of these villages ensures sustainable growth, strong local leadership, and resilience against both famine and invasion.
swedish_tradition: Forming our marching troops into a Svinfylking and charging is enough force to shatter any opponent! Mounted troops are not superior; other than being ridden to the battle itself, horses have no place on the battlefield.
swedish_heritage: Swedish peasants have always made significant contributions to our country; the differences between a noble and a free farmer have never been big.
kung_och_riksdag: Swedish rulers often depended on cooperation with the estates, especially with such a large peasant class compared to that of the nobility. During the reign of Gustavus Adolphus, however, a historic compromise was made with the aristocrats, who loyally pledged their resources to the disposal of the nation in return for new privileges.
swedish_steel: While other armies may be content to wildly fire inaccurate volleys at their enemies, we shall march at them in disciplined ranks, deliver a single volley at close range, and then feed them cold steel.
mulltimmer_masugn: Swedish Iron, prized for its purity and strength, supplies not only our domestic needs but also the foundries and armories of nations across the continent. The Mulltimmer Masugn was not built just with stone, but also with wood isolated with sand, gravel and dirt.
swedish_royal_post_office: The Kungliga Postverket, or Royal Postal Agency, was created to improve state administration and communication across the expanse of Sweden. It establishes a reliable network of couriers and waystations, and has become crucial for our military coordination, diplomacy, and governance.
swedish_copper_coins: The abundance of copper in Sweden, primarily from the Stora Kopparberget mine in Falun, has prompted the country to use it as the main metal for minting a new national currency, the daler. This is issued as a large money plate, called plåtmynt, which can weigh up to 20 kilograms. Some argue that this might not be very practical and that the volume of money in circulation could exceed copper reserves, but they seem narrow-minded.
indelningsverket: The Swedish allotment system divides the peasantry into groups of ten for recruitment purposes. This system made it easier to find people to serve in the army and organize them into units.
hakkapelitta: Finland is considered a rather poor and backwards region, but service in the Swedish cavalry offers skilled Finnish horsemen ample opportunities for glory and plunder. Superior horsemanship and high-quality mounts allow us to raise the feared Hakkapeliitta — cavalry so effective in battle that our enemies whisper they must be protected by witchcraft.
caroleans_advance: The Caroleans are the Swedish and Finnish infantry of the Swedish Empire. Recruited from the peasantry, the Caroleans go under strict training and are renowned for invoking fear in the hearts of their enemies.
swedish_absolutism: Absolutism is the theory that one person should be in charge, that this person is the monarch, and that said monarch shall run the government unfettered by the Privy Council.
polhem_machina_nova: Christopher Polhem, dubbed the 'father of Swedish engineering, has transformed Swedish industry with his Machina Nova, an innovative array of mechanical systems designed to streamline and boost production. Using intricate systems of gears, cams, and water power, Polhem has developed several machines capable of performing tasks previously done by hand, from ore-crushing in mines to textile weaving and sawmilling.
produktplakatet: The decree forbids foreign ships arriving in Sweden to bring goods from countries other than their own or their colonies.
teu_crusader_discipline: Our grand order was forged in the flames and blood of the Third Crusade during the siege of Acre in 1191. While we originally nursed the sick and feeble, the order has transformed into a militarized group of knights of unbreakable devotion and discipline.
teu_teutonic_heavy_cavalry: There is no greater symbol of power and military prowess than the heavy cavalry. While for many states the cavalry is made of nobles, every Teutonic Knight is also a member of our heavy cavalry, and undergoes the strict training of a crusader.
teu_reformed_order_army: The German knights, and veterans of the Crusades and other wars are simply not numerous enough to remain the base of our armies. We must reorganize the army to incorporate domestic levies, regiments capable of replacing the knights on the battlefield.
teu_peasants_recruitment: It has become clear to us that we can no longer rely on foreign volunteers to fill up our army ranks, no matter how experienced and valuable they might be. Instead, we will develop a system that would allow us to levy our subjects, both German and non-German folk alike.
teu_infantry_tactics: Contemporary battles in Europe have proven that the age of infantry is about to begin. It is now time to develop new tactics, adopt use of the pike, and reform our medieval concept of auxiliary infantry into the main fighting force of our future armies.
teu_teutonic_religious_authority: We will put an end to the loose religious autonomy local bishops hold within our realm. All religious matters, from taxation to converting the populace, will be state matters from now on.
teu_expanded_marches: Grant autonomy to the local governors of our border regions, and reform their holdings into marches. These special zones will pay fewer taxes to the state in return for an obligation to maintain the highest combat readiness during times of war as well as peace. This should provide us with substantial military flexibility at little cost.
teu_prussian_bishops: We shall grant further rights and privileges to our Prussian bishops, ensuring their loyalty in all matters.
teu_one_state_one_religion: Reserve all state offices only for those who follow our religion. Heretics and heathens are no longer welcome in our realm.
teu_absolute_order: All powers of the state are consolidated in our order. Every action taken and every decision made goes through the hierarchy of the Teutonic Order first before it gets executed. Of course, this bureaucracy is not in everyone's favor, but it ensures the absolute power of the Hochmeister.
sakya_hegemony: For the last century, the Sakya school has held temporal authority over Tibet, acting as spiritual and political stewards under Mongol patronage. Their dominance ushered in an age of centralized governance and scholastic consolidation. Though their rule has waned, their legacy continues to shape our approach to authority and order.
monastic_dominance: A fusion of spiritual and temporal rule defines our political landscape. From the smallest village to the halls of power in Sakya, monastic institutions are central to every sphere of life. Their moral authority and organizational prowess ensure loyalty, unity, and cultural resilience.
the_yak: Domesticated for centuries, the yak is the backbone of Tibetan pastoral life. It provides meat, milk, wool, transport, and fuel — even its dried dung is a vital source of fuel on the treeless plateau. In times of need or celebration, yak butter fills our lamps and cups.
drokpa: The Drokpa nomads often operate as herders and traders, porters that connect distant settlements. Through their traditions and unparalleled knowledge of the terrain, they traverse the high-altitude routes between Tibet, Bhutan, Ladakh, and Nepal. Their seasonal caravans carry Salt, Wool, and dried meat in exchange for grain and manufactured goods. These networks knit our mountains into a vibrant lattice of commerce and diplomacy.
tibetan_monastic_education: Our monastic institutions have long served as centers of learning, debate, and spiritual discipline. Through rigorous training and a structured approach to education, our clerics maintain a high standard of intellectual and moral integrity. These foundations will support wise governance and cultural flourishing across our enlightened realm.
tanye_guanxi: For centuries, our spiritual influence in China has formed the bedrock of our diplomatic relations. Imperial patronage, tribute exchanges, and sacred rituals like Tányuè secure both respect and material gain.
great_three: Sera, Ganden, and Drepung, these towering monastic universities form the intellectual heart of Tibet. Their scholars train one generation after another of monks, diplomats, and rulers. With their rise, our realm became not only a bastion of faith but a cradle of rigorous thought and institutional progress.
timurid_cavalry: As the great Genghis Khān dominated the steppes with the power of his cavalry, so will we triumph through our incomparable horses. Bred for the most rigorous combat, and mounted by the best-trained soldiers in the world, our cavalry will instill fear in the hearts of our enemies.
timurid_architecture: The architecture of Persia has been the envy of the known world for centuries. We must promote a new form of architecture, one that surpasses anything seen before, so that we may claim our birthright as the master of this art.
the_mantle_of_the_great_khan: The death of Genghis Khān created a power vacuum that led to people who should have known better vying to replace him. However, through strategic marriages, we have consolidated our claim to descent from the Great Khān himself, and the warriors of the steppes will declare their loyalty to us accordingly.
turco_persian_tradition: Persia has always been the undeniable center of culture and language in the region, influencing the different Turkic peoples that have been around for centuries. We will embrace this blend of cultures to create our own unique tradition.
tamerlane_chess: This new variety of chess, invented by our great eponymous founder, improves upon previous versions. Using it will help our generals to improve their strategic and tactical skills.
chagatai_literature: The Karluk language of the eastern steppes is far more worthy to carry the thoughts and ideas of our great lineage than Persian or Arabic ever could be. We must promote the use of our ancestral language, and create a new literary tradition.
nambardar_levy: The Nambardar Levy, or čerig-i nambardar, refers to our troops that do not come from Mongolian or Turkic origins, but instead come from the native Iranian population. Thanks to them, we can build larger armies than would have been possible before.
timurid_renaissance: Ever since the initial Timurid expansion, our realm has attracted the greatest artisans and wise men of the age. Through our continued patronage of art, science, and literature, we have made the cities of Herāt and Samarkand the brightest jewels in the world.
riches_of_the_silk_road: As long as our merchants control the trade through the lands of Transoxiana and Samarkand, the trade of the Silk Road shall flow unhindered and the wealth of our dynasty will continue to grow.
reform_the_diwan: We are fortunate to be served by loyal and well-educated Farsi administrators, who have perfected the art of governance for generations. Sadly, however, a hereditary office is one that over time might stagnate and lack innovation. By reducing the number of inherited offices with each generation, we can make sure that we reward not only loyalty, but also ability. Able administrators must rise to high positions regardless of which family they come from.
conquerors_legacy: Our glorious empire emerged from the legacy of great conquerors. It was the ferocity of Genghis Khān's troops that allowed him to conquer from Europe to China. As his successors, our troops will be as fearsome as the ones in his army.
tamazight: The Amazigh-speaking communities, from Jerba and the Matmata highlands in the east, through the Zenata confederations of the high plateaus, to the menceyatos of the Canary archipelago in the Atlantic, preserve the Tamazight language family, customary law, and pastoral wool economy that long predate the Arab and Castilian conquests of the wider region. Our weavers turn the long staples of mainland and island flocks into the rugged textiles, tent panels, and burnouses that no urban industry can match, while our tribal councils and menceys maintain a parallel system of customary justice independent of any external jurisprudence. For the Berber-rooted communities, from the Saharan oases to the Atlantic islands, a dual cultural and economic inheritance of language, livestock, and textiles runs parallel to and independent of the urban Maghrebi and Iberian mainstreams.
ahg_hoggar_massif: The Hoggar volcanic massif (Tahat, Assekrem, Atakor) provides our central Saharan refuge where our paramount confederation gathers and from which we project authority across the surrounding plains of salt and sand. Our tribal pastures circle the massif, and our migration routes between summer highland and winter lowland traverse it predictably. Garrison towers atop the peaks command sightlines hundreds of kilometers into the open desert. The mountain heartland is the Kel Ahaggar confederation's defensible core, beyond the reach of any purely plains Tuareg rival.
ait_beni_abbas_confederation: The Banū 'Abbās clan confederation of Lower Kabylia unites the highland villages of the Bibans range under a single hereditary chieftaincy, binding the assembled tajmā'āt to its founding family through marriage alliances, ritual oaths, and the religious and judicial mediation of the maraboutic shayḵs. Our chiefs claim descent from a single sharifian founder and convene the confederation's elders at the central fortified citadel for deliberation on war and peace. A dynastic and religious foundation keeps our highland federation politically continuous, unlike the looser Kabyle confederations to our west.
ajj_tassili_rock_art: The Tassili n'Ajjer plateau, adorned with prehistoric rock paintings of cattle herds, hunters, and ritual scenes from the Saharan-Neolithic period, provides our confederation with a deep cultural and archaeological inheritance that predates every dynasty of the Maghreb. Our ulema interpret the surviving inscriptions, and oral tradition preserves the names and significance of every major rock art site. Scholarly families keep manuscript records of the older Saharan past alongside the Islamic canon. The rock art gives the Kel Ajjer a cultural and historical depth rooted in our own soil, which no other Tuareg confederation can claim.
btl_atlas_pastoralism: Our confederation thrives on the transhumant pastoralism of the Tellian Atlas. Sheep, goats, and camels move seasonally between the upland summer pastures of the Aurès and the winter lowlands of the Constantine plain, sustained by a kinship economy that purely agricultural states cannot replicate. Our tribal chiefs hold their authority through the seasonal grazing rights they negotiate among the constituent clans, and our pastoral wealth supports a tribal warrior class whose flocks travel as both wealth and rations. Pastoralism holds the tribesmen loyal to the state and brings a prosperity independent of the rain-fed harvests.
cnr_tagoror_councils: The tagoror convenes our island's household heads, the achimencey nobility, and the elders of every clan at the sacred stone enclosures of each menceyato to deliberate water rights, herd movements, and the response to any vessel that lands on our shores. Decisions taken at the assembly bind every clan that participated and are preserved only in the oral memory of the gathered elders rather than in any written register vulnerable to outside seizure. This deliberative tradition spares our menceyato the costs of suppressing every petty dispute and binds the rural majority of our population to decisions they helped reach.
dje_ibadi_refuge: Our oases (Tozeur, Nefta, Douz, El Hamma, and the smaller settlements of the Chott) serve as one of the last refuges of the Ibāḍiyya tradition in the eastern Maghreb, sheltering Khārijī-Ibadi survivors from the doctrinal conflicts of the early Islamic centuries. Our clergy maintains the distinctive Ibadi fiqh alongside the surrounding Mālikī majority, preserving a tolerance and a religious autonomy unusual in the Sunni-dominated regions. Ibadi tolerance and an established clergy give our oases a steadfast religious life.
fez_qarawiyyin_school: The University of al-Qarawiyyīn, founded in 859 by Fāṭima al-Fihrī and continuously operating since, teaches the four Sunni schools of law, Aristotelian logic, astronomy, and medicine to scholars who arrive from every corner of the western Mediterranean. Ibn Khaldūn, Maimonides, and the chancellors of every Marinid sultan are among the alumni whose careers our halls have launched. An unbroken scholarly tradition quickens learning at our court and raises a literate class beyond what any younger Maghrebi institution can.
gbs_coastal_oasis: Our unique geography of sea and oasis, with palm groves growing within sight of the Mediterranean shore on the Gulf of Gabes, supports a rare combination of date palm production, citrus orchards, henna gardens, and sea fishing in the same agrarian unit. Our peasants harvest dates in autumn, sail for tuna in spring, and trade across both the Saharan and the Mediterranean trade circuits without ever leaving our oasis hinterland. Where coast meets oasis, our state enjoys richer harvests and a steadier prosperity than purely inland oases can know.
iwl_sahel_pastoral_economy: Our confederation occupies the Sahel-Tuareg space, the seasonal grassland between the central Saharan dunes and the Niger valley wetlands, where our pastoral economy combines cattle, sheep, and the date palm groves of the small surrounding oases. Our migration routes follow the rains north and south on an annual cycle. Customary agreements with surrounding sedentary populations bound our tribal confederation pastures, and a seasonal grain trade with the Niger-valley farming communities supplements our food supply. Blending Sahel and pastoral life gives the Iwellemmeden an economic base of livestock and grain, distinct from both the purely Saharan and the purely Sahel-sedentary economies.
kah_adrar_ifoghas: The Adrar des Ifoghas, the granite massif rising from the Mali-Algerian Sahara, provides our confederation with a fortress landscape of caves, narrow defiles, and elevated pasture that no invader's regular army can sweep without losing months and battles. Resident shrine keepers maintain the Sufi-marabout lodges scattered through the massif, and our caves shelter both refugee pastures during invasion and Quranic schools during peacetime. From this defensible heartland the paramount draws confederation-wide loyalty. The Adrar is both our fortress and our sanctuary, a place where the confederation can always withdraw, pray, and recover.
kay_air_massif: The Aïr volcanic massif, the granite peaks rising from the central Sahara south of the Hoggar and north of the Niger bend, provides our confederation with the elevated pasture and watered valley heartland that supports our settled population during the southerly migrations of the surrounding clans. Our paramount draws confederation-wide loyalty from this stronghold. Village settlements cluster on the upland valley sites, while peripheral camp clans cycle through the massif's pastures on a customary calendar. The mountain refuge gives the Kel Ayr a defensible warrior heartland and steadfast garrisons, which open desert territory could never supply to the more nomadic Tuareg confederations.
kgs_agropastoral_economy: Our confederation occupies the southernmost Tuareg territory, the agricultural and pastoral frontier where Saharan-Tuareg pastoralism meets the rain-fed Hausa agricultural plain, practicing a distinctive agropastoral economy that combines millet farming, cattle herding, and seasonal labor exchange with neighboring Hausa communities. Our pastoralists settle for part of the year alongside our farmers, and marriage alliances cross Tuareg-Hausa lines on a regular basis. Economic risk pooling spans both pastoral and agricultural sectors. Blending farming and herding gives the Kel Gres an economic foundation unique among the Tuareg, unlike the nomadic and pastoral confederations of the central Sahara.
kuk_djurjura_strongholds: The high citadels of the Djurdjura range (the central fortress village of Koukou, the Beni Yenni armorers' quarter, and the chain of ridge top fortifications across the Greater Kabylia) anchor our kingdom on terrain no flatland army can effectively reach. Our garrison engineers maintain the curtain walls, the cisterns, and the powder magazines through hereditary corvée obligations that bind every village to the central seat. These concentrated mountain fortresses let our state withstand sieges and keep its garrisons growing, as purely lowland kingdoms cannot at our altitudes.
mrk_almoravid_ribat_tradition: Our crown inherits the discipline of the al-Murābiṭūn, the warrior monks of Yūsuf ibn Tāshfīn whose fortified ribāṭ communities founded Marrakesh in the eleventh century as a base for both holy war and ascetic piety. The Almoravid ulema retain a presence in our great mosques and madrasas that older dynasties cannot match, lending our sultan the moral standing of a successor to the founders rather than a merely civil ruler. This inherited religious and military identity binds our clergy and our warrior nobility to the throne through a shared founding narrative no rival Maghrebi capital can claim.
mzb_pentapolis_foundation: The five fortified Ibadi cities of the M'zab valley (Ghardaïa, Beni Isguen, Bou Noura, Melika, and El Atteuf) rise above the Wādī M'zab as a refuge for the Ibadi survivors of the Rustamid kingdom destroyed at Tāhart in 909. Each city is built as a fortified qṣar with its mosque tower serving as both minaret and watchtower, governed by the consensus of its founding families and bound to its sisters by intermarriage and a shared halqa al-'azzāba religious council. The pentapolis leaves our Ibadi community an urban heritage of walls and towers that no other Saharan settlement can claim.
ogl_saharan_terminus: Our oasis sits at the northern terminus of the great trans-Saharan caravan routes coming up from Gao, Timbuktu, and the Niger bend. Every Soninke, Songhay, and Tuareg merchant arriving from the south must clear customs at our gates before pushing on to the Mediterranean. Our caravanserais (Sidi Lakhdar, Sidi Boumendil, the fanādiq of the central market) host the caravan crews and their pack animals for the months between expeditions, and our brokers arrange onward shipment to Algiers, Tunis, and Tripoli. At the terminus, our state takes a commanding share of the trans-Saharan trade revenues, which no maritime power can dispute.
qalat_al_mashwar_advance: The Qal'at al-Mashwar at the heart of Tlemcen rises as both fortified royal residence and the seat of Zayyanid court ceremony, housing the dīwān that taxes the Saharan caravans from Sijilmasa and Ouargla, the Mediterranean shipping from Oran, and the overland passage between Fez and Tunis. Its triple-walled enclosure concentrates the offices of state, including administrative chambers, the mint, the markets of the Mechouar quarter, and the sultan's personal guard, within a single defensible compound. A stronghold at once palace and treasury lends the Zayyanid capital a fiscal weight beyond any purely territorial Maghrebi state, and the strength that comes from holding every organ of state behind the same walls.
sos_taroudant_garrison_seat: The red ramparts of Tārūdānt, the longest continuously garrisoned fortified circuit in the Sus valley, enclose our barracks, our magazine quarter, our armory, and our cavalry stables within a single defensible compound that has rebuffed every besieger to test it since the Almoravid age. Our garrison engineers maintain the curtain walls, the bastions, and the powder cellars from a permanent corvée of skilled masons who hold their offices as hereditary trusts in exchange for tax exemption. These concentrated fortifications let our crown maintain its fortifications across the Sus at a fraction of the upkeep that scattered frontier garrisons would require.
tat_date_palmery: Millions of date palms across the Tuat oases, sustained by the foggāra irrigation networks running tens of kilometers under the desert sand, feed our people, our caravans, and our export trade in equal measure. Our cultivators have selected the celebrated Deglet Nour and Aghras varieties for premium markets across the Mediterranean and the Sahel. Deep oasis cultivation brings our crown a great export of fruit and a steady prosperity that the rain-fed agriculture of the Maghrebi coast can never match.
tfl_sijilmasa_gold_terminus: Every caravan from the Sahel terminates its journey at Sijilmāsa, the great trans-Saharan way station at the heart of Tafilalt where Wangara gold dust, Sudanic kola, and Saharan captives change hands for slab salt, Maghrebi textiles, and the silver of the Iberian Mediterranean. Our merchant clans operate the assay foundries, the gold dust scales, and the bonded warehouses through hereditary charters that secure the prosperity of the entire oasis. Our unbroken commercial primacy fills the Tafilalt with the wealth of the southern caravans, a prosperity that inland Maghrebi cities far from the desert termini cannot match.
tgt_saharan_crossroads: Our oasis sits at the confluence of three trans-Saharan caravan routes (the western route to Tafilalt and Sijilmasa, the central route to Ouargla and the Niger, and the eastern route to Ghadāmis and Tripoli), making us the natural meeting point for caravans of every Maghrebi state. Our central market draws traders from Tunis, Algiers, Fez, Tripoli, and the deep Sahara every season, and the migrant families who follow the caravans settle in our growing urban quarters. Standing at the crossroads, our state reaches across the entire Saharan network and draws a steady stream of settlers to its towns, as no single-route oasis can.
trg_tin_hinan_legacy: The legendary Tīn Hinān, founding ancestress of the Kel Ahaggar whose royal tomb at Abalessa we still tend, anchors a matrilineal inheritance custom that traces noble status, herd ownership, and ceremonial rank through the female line. Our amenokals each claim descent through their mother's clan from Tīn Hinān herself, and our succession disputes are settled in her cosmic authority. This matrilineal legitimacy binds our nobles to the throne by an inheritance system no patrilineal Maghrebi neighbor can disrupt or replicate.
amazigh_group_agraw_council: Our village assemblies (the agraw in the Kabyle highlands, the jma'a across the Maghreb, the tagrart among the Saharan confederations, and the tagoror of the Canary menceyatos) convene the household heads to deliberate water rights, herd movements, blood money settlements, and the response to any external authority that presents itself at our gates. Decisions taken in council bind every clan that participated and are recorded in the oral memory of the assembled imghassen elders rather than in any written register vulnerable to royal seizure. This deliberative practice spares our crown the costs of suppressing every petty dispute and binds the rural majority of our population to decisions they helped reach.
ahg_abalessa_seat: The fortress of Abalessa, where the ancestral queen Tīn Hinān is entombed, anchors the political and religious authority of our paramount line. Our amenokal accession ceremonies take place at the fortress walls, and our ulema pilgrimage to the tomb at appointed seasons. Court records of every paramount chief succession reference the Abalessa rites as the formal investiture. The sacred political seat anchors our confederation's authority for the long term, which the more loosely organized Saharan rivals cannot do.
ait_kabyle_marabouts: The local marabouts, wandering Sufi shayḵs and their settled descendants, anchor the religious and judicial life of our confederation, arbitrating clan disputes, certifying marriages, and binding the scattered villages to the central chieftaincy through shared baraka. Our crown patronizes the lodges of the Sidi Ahmed Bel Qasim school and the older Qādiriyya families, and our religious establishment gains a depth that purely tribal mountain confederations rarely achieve. Maraboutic authority extends our state's reach in faith and law across our territory, beyond any purely secular chieftaincy.
ajj_ghat_oasis: The oasis of Ghat, at the eastern Hoggar foothills near the Acacus Mountains, serves as our principal town of caravans and settlers, supporting date palms, oasis gardens, and the resident merchant families that intermediate the Saharan caravan trade. Irrigated garden plots produce fruit and vegetables that no surrounding desert can supply. Our caravanserais host the seasonal trans-Saharan traffic, and customs revenue funds the confederation's central treasury. The oasis town anchors the Kel Ajjer with an agricultural and commercial base that the more purely pastoral Tuareg rivals lack.
btl_constantine_hinterland: Our confederation occupies the immediate hinterland of the great fortress city of Constantine, supplying the city's grain, wool, leather, and livestock markets while our chiefs negotiate caravan protection and toll immunity treaties with whichever power holds the city. Our merchant houses ride the constant trade of the Constantine markets, and our envoys gain experience negotiating with the central courts of Algeria and Tunisia alike. Standing in the hinterland of a great city gives our state a merchant's reach and a diplomatic experience unknown to purely mountain confederations far from the cities.
cnr_silbo_signal_tongue: Our shepherds and watchmen master the whistled Silbo, a transposition of our Guanche speech into pure tones that carry across the deep barrancos of Guanche where no spoken voice can reach. A sentinel atop one ridge passes word of approaching strangers, fleets on the horizon, or assembly summonses to the next ridge in moments rather than the hours a runner would require. Our whistled signals warn our court early and carry secret messages that no foreign intelligence service can decipher or intercept.
dje_djerid_marabouts: The local Sufi marabouts of the Djerid, combining Ibadi religious orthodoxy with practical wisdom in oasis water rights, palm grove inheritance, and caravan protection ritual, anchor the religious and judicial life of our oasis cities through their permanent lodges and seasonal pilgrimage festivals. Our crown endows the shrines of the great founding shayḵs and patronizes the teaching circles of their living successors. The blend of Ibadi and Sufi traditions lends our clergy a depth and moral authority across the southern oases, beyond that of purely imported orders.
entrepot_connections: Our roads link Tlemcen to its outport of Honein on the Mediterranean, to the Saharan staging post of Sijilmasa, and to the great Maghrebi trunk routes that cross our territory under royal escort. We charter our noble houses to maintain the carriage tracks and the funduq stations along these arteries in exchange for tax exemptions and grants of land along the route. This system of merchant convoys keeps the central Maghrebi trade flowing reliably even when factional warfare disrupts Fez or Tunis.
fez_brassworkers_guild: The Fassi brass and copper guilds, concentrated in the Seffarine quarter, produce the inlaid lamps, trays, astrolabes, and hammered platters that command premium prices from Genoese, Pisan, and Venetian buyers at the Mediterranean fairs. Master-apprentice chains of training transmit the chasing, repoussé, and silver inlay techniques through generations of Fassi households. The regulated metal craft gives our crown a trade in copper wares and a class of artists, beyond what the wool and leather producers of the inland Maghreb can offer.
gbs_gulf_anchorage: Our natural harbor on the Gulf of Gabes, sheltered by the Kerkennah islands, deep enough for Mediterranean galleys, and supplied with fresh water from the oasis itself, supports a fleet of coastal galleys and a sailor pool drawn from our oasis and coastal inhabitants in equal measure. Our shipwrights train in the techniques of both the eastern Mediterranean galley building and the Saharan caravan camel husbandry that our hinterland requires. Our anchorage on the Gulf draws a steady stream of sailors and builds a tradition of the sea unknown to purely inland oases.
iwl_niger_valley_rights: Our confederation negotiates formal access rights to the Niger-valley floodplain pastures with the resident Songhay, Fulani, and Soninke populations, securing the dry-season grazing that our flocks depend on through diplomatic agreements between our paramount and their chiefs rather than through force. Our envoys hold standing positions in the Niger-bend market towns, and our migration timing is coordinated with the Niger's cycle of flood and recession. At each major succession on both sides, the paramount renews the pasture access compacts. Our pasture agreements along the Niger keep our flocks alive, as desert resources alone could never do for purely Saharan Tuareg confederations.
kah_niger_pasture_rights: Our confederation negotiates seasonal rights to pasture and water with the Songhai and post-Songhai sedentary populations along the Niger bend, moving our flocks south to the inundated floodplain pastures during the dry season and back north to the Adrar uplands during the rains. Our paramount maintains formal envoy relationships with the Niger-bend chiefs, and our migration arrangements are recorded in both sides' customary law. Our pastoral economy depends on this annual rhythm. Access to the Niger-bend pastures extends the economic and territorial reach of the Kel Adagh beyond that of purely Saharan Tuareg confederations.
kay_agadez_sultanate: The Sultanate of Agadez, founded by the Tuareg-elected paramount and ratified by the surrounding nobility, establishes our confederation as a formal kingdom rather than a tribal chieftaincy. Our sultan receives investiture at the central mosque, and succession protocols are codified in customary law. Our court receives envoys from the Songhai, Hausa, and Maghrebi states on a peer sovereign basis. As a sultanate, the Kel Ayr is recognized as a true state, a standing no other Tuareg confederation claims for the period.
kgs_hausa_synthesis: Our confederation's identity emerges from the long Tuareg-Hausa cultural and linguistic contact: bilingual households where Tamasheq and Hausa coexist, hybrid religious practices that integrate Tuareg customary law with Hausa Islamic jurisprudence, and shared kinship networks that span the Niger-Hausa boundary. Our ulema and our Hausa marabout neighbors exchange students and texts. Marriage practices cross linguistic lines, and Tuareg and Hausa observers alike recognize our distinctive cultural form as a third culture. Blending two peoples gives the Kel Gres an identity that reaches across both worlds, as no purely Tuareg or purely Hausa rival can.
kuk_belkadi_dynasty: The Belkadi house of Koukou consolidates the scattered Kabyle confederations under a single royal line, drawing legitimacy from sharifian descent claims, from marabout endorsements at the foundation ceremony, and from the assembled tajmā'āt of every constituent village. Our chancery records the royal decrees and tax registers, our court ceremonial draws on both Marinid administrative practice and Kabyle custom, and our dynasty consolidates a centralized monarchy that the consensus-governed neighboring Kabyle confederations never achieve. The royal foundation gives our state a court that governs well and a religious and dynastic legitimacy beyond that of purely tribal chieftaincies.
mrk_atlas_caravan_terminus: Every caravan crossing the High Atlas from the Drâa, the Sus, or the Saharan termini at Sijilmasa breaks its journey at Marrakesh. The Bāb Aghmāt and the southern walls of our city host the funduq stations, watering reservoirs, and customs posts where each load is registered and taxed. Our merchant houses extend credit to the desert merchants in the Saharan currencies and accept return payment in the goods unloaded at our gates, knitting the trans-Saharan and Mediterranean economies through a single set of accounting books. As a terminus, Marrakesh fills the treasury with a steady transit revenue and gives our merchant burghers a lasting commercial advantage over inland Maghrebi cities further from the mountain passes.
mzb_ibadi_seclusion: Our communities practice the doctrine of taqiyya (precautionary dissimulation) when interacting with Sunni-majority neighbors, professing common Sunni forms in public while maintaining strict Ibadi orthodoxy within the pentapolis walls. Our women are veiled and confined to the home courtyards, our markets segregate visitors from the inner sacred spaces, and our jurists publicly defer to the Mālikī fatwās of Algiers and Tunis while privately following their own al-Madhhab al-Wahbī line. This doctrine of religious and cultural seclusion preserves our distinct Ibadi identity through centuries of Sunni political pressure that have erased every other Khārijī community.
ogl_in_salah_route: Our caravan masters establish the Ouargla to Niger Bend route as the dominant central Saharan trade route, supplanting the older route from Sijilmasa through the western Sahara as the preferred path for our merchants. We maintain the In Salah staging post jointly with Tuareg confederations, each side providing guards, water rights guarantees, and warehouse space, and our jurists formalize the customs and toll schedules at every staging post. This ordered route, with its guards, wells, and fixed tolls, carries our merchants across the Sahara farther than any other oasis state can reach.
sos_jazuli_sufi_movement: The Ṭarīqa Jazūliyya, founded in our southern hinterland by Muḥammad b. Sulaymān al-Jazūlī (whose Dalā'il al-Khayrāt becomes the most-copied Maghrebi devotional text of the late medieval era), spreads through the zawāyā of Sus, the Drâa, and the Sus before its missionaries carry it to every Maghrebi capital. Our court patronizes the Jazūlī shayḵs at their lodge in Afoughal, endows their teachers, and receives their blessing at each accession ceremony in turn. The Sufi renewal binds our urban clergy and our rural marabouts to the throne through a single revivalist current and lends our sultanate a religious legitimacy that the older established orders will struggle to counter.
tat_maghili_jurisprudence: Muḥammad al-Maghīlī of Tuat, author of the Aḥkām Ahl adh-Dhimma and counselor to the askiyas of Songhai, exports our Mālikī jurisprudence across the western Sahara, the Hausa cities, and the Sahel kingdoms beyond. His rulings on dhimmī status, taxation, and ruler-subject obligations bind the courts of Songhai, Kano, and Katsina to Tuat's juridical authority. This concentrated scholarly authority extends our cultural influence well beyond our oasis frontiers and binds the southern Maghrebi-Sahelian clergy to our shayḵs.
tfl_oasis_levy_horsemen: Each ksar of Tafilalt provides its share of the seasonal horse and mehari camel rider muster, a light cavalry of the Saharan school trained from boyhood to ride down raiders across the dunes, ambush caravans, and outpace any pursuing force across terrain no infantry can cover. Our oasis stables breed the dark-coated Berber horse on the date palm fodder of our gardens and on the brackish wells of the deep oasis, producing mounts of stamina that no Mediterranean-bred warhorse can match in the Saharan climate. Our oasis cavalry tradition fields a swift mobile force whose endurance and speed the standing forces of the centralizing northern courts will struggle to meet.
tgt_caravan_levies: Our crown raises a permanent military garrison through caravan tax revenues. The zakāt al-'ushūr on incoming goods funds standing oasis guard companies and a tribal cavalry reserve drawn from the surrounding Berber confederations. Our tribesmen serve in rotation on the city walls and at the caravan staging waterholes, earning a share of caravan fees in lieu of regular pay, and our crown's permanent military establishment grows independent of either central Algerian or Tunisian tributary demands. Funded by the caravans, our levy system gives our state a standing garrison at no cost to the regular agricultural economy.
trg_caravan_protection_levies: Every caravan crossing our Saharan territory pays the Tuareg teggama protection tariff, at rates the amenokal's heralds publish at every waterpost, in exchange for safe passage past the raiding clans of the deeper desert. Our escort detachments are drawn from every confederation through standing clan oaths, and the tariff revenue circulates back through the same kin network as redistribution to the tents that supplied the riders. An open, published protection tariff brings our crown a steady income from the caravans and keeps the clans bound together, something no settled state could wring from our migration paths.
amazigh_group_igherman: Our settlements take the form of the igherman, the fortified stone villages adapted to each landscape we inhabit: the rammed earth qasbah of the High Atlas, the layered ksar of the southern oases, the tower house taddart of the Kabyle peaks, and the walled tagoror of the Canary uplands. Each settlement is built communally by the families who will occupy it, with shared granaries, watchtowers, and refuge cisterns concentrated within walls that an attacker cannot afford to siege one by one across our entire territory. This dispersed defensive architecture makes our heartlands disproportionately expensive to invade and bleeds any imperial campaign long before its main force has accomplished anything.
ahg_tamanrasset_caravan: The Tamanrasset oasis at the Hoggar's southern foot serves as the principal caravan terminus between the Maghrebi north and the Aïr-Niger south. Our merchant houses provision the southbound legs with grain and cloth, and our customs officers tax the through traffic at fixed rates. The Hoggar quarries feed the exchange of salt and millet that keeps the corridor profitable. As a caravan terminus, Tamanrasset earns a trading income that the more isolated Saharan oases cannot draw from passing traffic alone.
ait_andalusi_smiths: Andalusi exile craftsmen (gunsmiths, copper workers, leather finishers, and engineers from Toledo, Granada, and Córdoba) find refuge in our Kalāa des Beni Abbas, bringing the metalworking and gunpowder craft of the lost peninsula to our mountain workshops. Our highland armories now produce arquebus barrels, copperware, and engraved firearms at a quality that no other Kabyle confederation can reach. The influx of Andalusi artisanship arms our crown with a corps of light infantry carrying firearms and a craft in copper that purely pastoral neighbors cannot field.
ajj_libyan_caravan_route: The caravan route running Ghat-Murzuk-Tripoli, the eastern Saharan corridor between sub-Saharan Africa and the Ottoman-Libyan coast, passes through our territory and pays our fees for tolls and protection at every major waypoint. Our caravan masters guide the through traffic, and our well-keepers maintain the watering stops at fixed intervals. At the northern terminus the paramount negotiates the toll rates with the Tripolitan and Fezzan authorities. The eastern route sets the Kel Ajjer on a commercial and diplomatic path of its own, distinct from the western corridor (Hoggar-Aïr) trade system.
btl_mountain_raiding: Our mounted light cavalry (drawn from the youngest sons of every clan, mounted on the swift Berber horses our pastoral economy raises) patrol the contested frontiers of our confederation, riding down rival raiders, extracting tribute from passing caravans, and gathering reputation in the cross-clan competitive games of the seasonal fairs. Our cavalry tradition transmits its tactical knowledge through hereditary apprenticeship within the warrior families. Our raiding tradition fills the state with swift riders and a soldiery that recovers quickly from setbacks, which the more sedentary Maghrebi states cannot reproduce through formal training.
cnr_dragon_tree_groves: Our island groves of Dracaena draco, the ancient dragon trees whose ruby-red resin Mediterranean apothecaries prize as sanguis draconis for medicines, varnishes, and altar paints, supply a luxury export no mainland producer can match. The Genoese cargo manifests of the late medieval Atlantic name our resin as the most reliable source between the Levant and the Indies, and our merchants control every grove on every island the menceyatos rule. The monopoly on our resin brings the crown a rich dye trade and a standing in European markets far beyond that of a purely agricultural archipelago.
dje_tozeur_madrasa: Our central madrasa at Tozeur (funded by the assembled palm grove rentier families and staffed by Ibadi and Mālikī teachers in equal measure) trains the scribes, judges, and missionaries of our oases through a curriculum that mediates between the two madhāhib and the broader Saharan scholarly tradition. Our graduates serve as qādīs across the Djerid, our students travel to Tunis and Cairo for advanced training, and our reputation for cross-doctrinal scholarship attracts pilgrim students from beyond our territory. Concentrated learning gives our state a more literate clergy and a wider reach among the southern oases than purely rural Ibadi communities enjoy.
fez_old_city_refortified: The Waṭṭāsid sultans rebuild the curtain walls of Fez al-Bālī and add the bastions of Fez al-Jdīd, anticipating the Sa'dī advance from the south through a generation of careful fortification work. Our garrison engineers maintain the gates of Bāb Bū Jelūd, the ramparts overlooking the Sebou plain, and the citadel of the kasbah, and the standing companies who hold them are recruited from the Fassi households on rotating service. Concentrating our military effort in these walls grows our garrisons steadily and builds a skill in siege engineering that scattered frontier posts never acquire.
gbs_henna_export: Our coastal oasis henna gardens, indigo plots, and saffron fields produce the dyes that European cloth finishers and Maghrebi tanneries demand in the highest grades, supplying the colorants for Andalusi-style tilework, Mediterranean wool dyeing, and our own coastal cotton industries. Our merchant houses control the bonded warehouses at the Gulf shore, and our brokers extend credit to the dye grove owners. Shipping agents route the export through Tunis, La Goulette, and the smaller Tunisian ports. Our dye exports fill the crown's coffers with the profits of a luxury trade and keep our merchants thriving.
iwl_hausa_trade_interface: Our southern frontier brings us into commercial contact with the Hausa city-states (Kano, Katsina, Zaria) whose markets we supply with desert salt and the Maghrebi cloth our caravans bring south, exchanging it for Sudanese gold, slaves, and the agricultural staples that our pastoral confederation cannot produce. Our caravan masters specialize in the Hausa-frontier routes, and our paramount maintains formal protocol with the Hausa emirs. Trade toll arrangements with the southern Hausa cities supplement our pastoral revenue substantially. Trade to the south broadens the commerce of the Iwellemmeden beyond that of the Tuareg confederations that look only to the north.
kah_songhai_borderlands: The Songhai-empire frontier (Timbuktu, Gao, and the eastern reaches of the empire) sees our confederation positioned as the principal Saharan frontier power, managing the trans-Saharan caravan traffic that brings Maghrebi salt south in exchange for Sudanese gold. Our paramount receives Songhai envoys at our negotiating stations. Caravan toll arrangements with the Niger-bend authorities are renewed at each succession, and formal Tuareg-Songhai cooperation keeps the trade routes secure. Standing at the empire's edge gives the Kel Adagh a commercial and diplomatic role that no purely internal Saharan confederation could play.
kay_salt_caravan_hub: Agadez serves as the principal caravan hub of the central Saharan corridor: the meeting point where the Bilma salt caravans from the east, the Maghrebi caravans of cloth and firearms from the north, and the Hausa caravans of grain and cloth from the south converge in a single market where three routes meet. Customs revenue from this through traffic dominates our state finances. Our caravanserais host the seasonal arrivals, and our merchant houses intermediate between the three routes. As the hub of the desert trade, the Kel Ayr lives on a trade that no purely pastoral confederation could sustain.
kgs_madaoua_settlements: The Madaoua area (the southern Niger market town belt where our agropastoral economy concentrates its settled population) hosts our confederation's principal urban centers, mixing Tuareg notable families with resident Hausa merchant-artisan populations in a distinctive hybrid urban culture. Market days bring together pastoralist sellers from the surrounding sahel, and our craft workshops specialize in the leather, metalwork, and textile production that no purely pastoral economy can support. Our notable families keep residences in both urban Madaoua and the surrounding pastoral camps. Madaoua and its settled towns give the Kel Gres a permanent seat of administration, which the more purely nomadic Tuareg confederations cannot have.
kuk_mountain_warfare_doctrine: Our highland combat doctrine, refined by generations of Kabyle warriors fighting on the steep Djurdjura slopes, the dense oak forests, and the broken ridge passes of the central kingdom, trains every village levy in tactics of ambush and retreat, in stealth movement across terrain no flatland infantry can navigate, and in the ridge-top signals that let dispersed companies coordinate without direct command. Our officers transmit the doctrine through hereditary apprenticeship within the warrior houses. Every village levy knows its own ridges, and an invader who climbs them pays for each one.
mrk_almoravid_dinar_mint: Our great dār as-sikka at the heart of Marrakesh continues the Almoravid practice of striking the celebrated Murābiṭ dinar, coins of an exceptionally pure gold standard, drawn from Wangara stock arriving at our gates by trans-Saharan caravan and refined in our own assay foundries. The reputation of the Marrakesh dinar carries beyond the Maghreb to the Genoese, the Pisan, and the Iberian markets, where it circulates at face value when lesser issues are weighed and discounted on every counting table. This monetary credibility lets our tax assessors collect at face value across the realm and lets our merchants maintain their accounts in a coin no rival mint can match.
mzb_ibadi_codification: Our scholars at Beni Isguen and Ghardaïa compile the great Ibadi-Wahbī jurisprudence, the Kitāb an-Nīl of Sheikh 'Abd al-'Azīz ath-Thamīnī, the legal commentaries of Atfayyash and Bābū, codifying centuries of fiqh al-'ibādiyya into a written reference corpus. We send our promising young students from each pentapolis city to the others to learn from the senior 'azzāba councils, and our scholarly graduates serve as judges, scribes, and missionaries across the broader Ibadi world from Oman to Zanzibar. Codification gives our religious establishment a depth and coherence within our sect that no Sunni-Maghrebi madrasa tradition can offer.
ogl_camel_caravan_corps: Our caravan protection auxiliary corps, the mehārist companies of mounted camel cavalry recruited from the Banū Wargla and the desert edge Berber tribes, patrol the southern approaches to our oasis, escorting incoming caravans through the Tassili and Tademaït plateaus where Tuareg raiders are most active. They serve under our crown on a contractual basis, paid through caravan toll revenues rather than the central treasury, and our officers integrate them as auxiliaries to the regular oasis garrisons during inter-state campaigns. The camel corps is a flexible Saharan striking force, able to range over long distances of desert where settled cavalry would founder.
sos_draa_warrior_emergence: The clans of the Drâa valley and Tagmadart (long-settled sharifian houses whose warriors have skirmished against coastal foreign incursions for generations) coalesce under the banner of Sus as a southern military federation drawing recruits from the entire pre-Saharan basin. Our muster grounds at Tagmadart, Taroudant, and Massa fill with mountain infantry, oasis cavalry, and arquebusiers trained in the new techniques captured from the coastal fortresses, all bound by oaths sworn under the baraka of the southern marabouts. This warrior emergence rebuilds our manpower base after each campaign with a speed and martial discipline the older established Maghrebi capitals cannot match.
tat_caravan_escort_corps: The Tuat escort companies, armed and mounted on oasis-bred camels and Saharan horses, hire out their services to every major caravan transiting our territory between Sijilmāsa and the Niger bend. Our riders know every waterhole, every reliable forage track, and every raider's likely ambush point across two thousand kilometers of desert. Our light cavalry escorts caravans swiftly and reinforces our campaigns quickly, for no inland Maghrebi power has our local knowledge of the desert.
tfl_caravan_protection_tariffs: The qā'ids of Tafilalt levy a regulated ṣadaqa al-qāfila (caravan protection tariff) on every load entering or departing the oasis at the published rates of our customs houses at Sijilmasa, Rissani, and the desert gates, in exchange for armed escort across the pre-Saharan frontier. The collection passes through bonded accountants of the qā'idal houses, with a fixed share routed directly to the central court and the remainder retained for the maintenance of the desert escort and the upkeep of the watering posts. This published rate tariff system stabilizes our exchange of caravan custom for state protection and routes the proceeds straight to the sultan's court, sparing our treasury the waste of provincial intermediaries.
tgt_beni_djellab_dynasty: The Beni Djellab family proclaim themselves Sultans of Touggourt, consolidating power over the Souf and Wādī Rīgh oasis complexes under a single dynastic line whose dynastic continuity outlasts every neighboring oasis confederation. They build the central Touggourt qaṣr as both ceremonial residence and administrative center, organize a makhzen-style chancery for fiscal records, and project authority across the surrounding ksūr through marriage alliances and military levies. The sultanate gives the Souf oasis region a centralized political form, which the consensus-governed neighboring oases never achieve.
tle_tlemcen_carpets: Our urban looms, concentrated in the Bāb al-'Aqaba and Bāb Sīdī Bū Madyan quarters, weave the celebrated sajjādat Tilimsān, the dense-knotted pile carpets whose geometric medallions distinguish them from every other Maghrebi rug tradition. Andalusi master weavers who settled in our city add new vegetal patterns and indigo vermilion palettes that command premium prices from Genoese, Marseillais, and Venetian merchants at the Oran fairs. Our regulated carpet industry gives our crown a trade in luxury cloth and an urban class of artisans, far beyond what the wool and tent producers of the inland tribes can offer.
trg_imuhagh_warrior_caste: The Imūhagh, noble warriors mounted on the finest mehari and trained from boyhood in the lance, the cross-hilted takūba sword, and the iron-pointed javelin, form our striking corps whose battlefield discipline no Sahelian army can answer. Their training camps at the Ahaggar wells and the Aïr highlands instill an arms mastery transmitted across generations. From this noble warrior tradition comes a light cavalry striking force of a kind that any sedentary state would need centuries to build.
amazigh_group_taqbilt_solidarity: The taqbilt, our network of patrilineal clans bound by descent from a shared apical ancestor, is the elementary unit of political life across every Amazigh confederation. A clan that has migrated abroad keeps its place in the home federation and reciprocates with envoys, intelligence, and the hospitality networks that knit our kin from Senegambia to Anatolia together. These kinship ties give our crown envoys and friends across the Maghreb, the Sahel, and the Mediterranean, a reach that transcends any individual ruler's authority and persists through every dynastic crisis.
ahg_amenokal_paramount: The amenokal (the paramount chief) exercises personal authority over the assembled confederation through a council of imashaghen nobles, the drum of office and other regalia, and ceremonial titulature that no Maghrebi sultan can equal in its specifically Tuareg form. Our paramount's word binds the assembled clans, our envoys carry the amenokal's seal in all negotiations of the confederation, and our administrative messengers transmit decisions from the central Hoggar to the peripheral clan camps within days. Under one supreme chief, the Kel Ahaggar can act decisively, as purely tribal Tuareg rivals seldom can.
ait_independence_from_lowland: Our highland geography, our maraboutic legitimacy, and our network of fortified citadels let us maintain political autonomy against every centralizing court that attempts to bring the Kabylia under direct rule. We negotiate as equals from the safety of our mountain redoubts, paying tribute when convenient and withholding it when not, while the central courts find their reach blunted by our terrain and our marabouts. Such independence makes our state hard to break and spares us much of the hostility of the lowland courts.
ajj_ahaggar_diplomacy: Our confederation maintains a careful diplomatic balance with the larger Kel Ahaggar to the west, exchanging marriage alliances, negotiating rights to pasture and water, and managing the inter-confederation disputes that any expanding Hoggar power would otherwise resolve by force. Our envoys hold standing positions at the Tamanrasset court, and our paramount accepts ritual primacy in some Hoggar ceremonial contexts while preserving our independence on substantive matters. Intermarriage keeps the two confederations bound by kin ties. This careful diplomacy lets the Kel Ajjer keep its independence beside a larger Saharan power, which no purely isolated small group of clans could manage.
btl_aures_marabouts: The maraboutic shayḵs of the Aurès, descended from the early medieval saints whose tombs anchor our highest pilgrimage sites, bind our scattered villages and our wandering pastoralist clans to a single religious and judicial network whose authority no purely secular chieftaincy can match. Our crown endows the lodge shrines, our chiefs receive their ijāza from the Aurès shayḵs, and our religious establishment gains the depth that comes from hereditary scholarly succession. Anchored in the Aurès, our spiritual authority keeps the clergy content and lends our government a legitimacy that flatland courts struggle to build.
