shared_brotherhood: United in the teachings of the Great Law of Peace, our people maintain a strong sense of brotherhood and unity, despite their disparate tribal background.
system_of_tributaries: Direct rule comes at the cost of extensive investment in subjugating and pacifying rival groups. By instead installing a loyal official to rule locally and demanding they pay an annual tribute, we eliminate threats from any rival Āltepētl while filling our treasury at the same time.
pyramid_architecture: Our ancestors constructed massive stone pyramids in the far-gone days of Teōtīhuacān, Tik'al, Copan, and Palenque. We have not forgotten the art of pyramid building, and can carry on this tradition.
ball_game: The heart of social life in our society is the ball game, where players strive to keep the ball inside the playing court by striking it with their hips. It is both a ritual alternative to warfare and a large part of religious life.
war_bonfires: A network of frontier settlements linked together by immense bonfires, which can be seen from a huge distance when lit, will allow us to quickly alert multiple settlements at once to threats, and therefore respond far faster.
merchant_officials: Merchants and their trading contribute substantially to our national income. However, merchants are also excellent sources of information, as they are often in the position to observe first-hand what circumstances our neighbors are in. By giving them official roles in the government, we can exploit their knowledge and mobility to our own ends.
copperworking: Our artisans have begun to craft tools out of Copper, a precious metal found throughout our territory. If we were to master this art, it would give us a tremendous advantage over our neighbors.
refined_obsidian_weaponry: Obsidian is an excellent material for making all kinds of tools and weapons. The hard, glasslike rock holds a sharp edge beautifully, making it an easy task to create blades, spearheads, or arrowheads which leave deadly wounds on any foe.
precious_stones_art: Our area is rich in precious stones, which are excellent for adding color, detail, and sparkle to artistic pieces and mundanities alike. Our craftsmen will immortalize themselves through these glittering jewels, and create great monuments to our culture.
cultivate_the_land: The jungle is a harsh environment in which to live, especially for farming cultures. Clearing portions of the jungle to create arable land is therefore one of our most vital tasks. We must organize our people in such a way that we can employ large labor forces to carry out these works whenever the need arises.
feathered_serpent: The legend of the Feathered Serpent is well-known across our lands. Although this figure represents many things to many people, such as Quetzalcōātl among the Nahua, K'uk'ulkan among the Maya or Q'uq'umatz among the K'iche', he is a unifying figure for all of them.
ritual_bloodletting: Many cultures in this region consider ritual sacrifice and bloodletting by the ruler as a way of paying homage to the gods. Maintaining this tradition pleases the gods and affirms our right to rule through divine tribute.
valley_irrigation: By building extensive networks of canals and connecting the waterways of our homeland's valleys, we can greatly improve our irrigation techniques and the productivity of our farmlands.
artisan_migration: It is not fitting that territories we have conquered should have better artisans and wiser advisors than in our capital. The greatest hands and minds of the empire must be brought to the capital to serve us directly.
terrace_farming: To take maximum advantage of the limited space in our highlands, we have developed terrace farming, a series of step-like platform fields on the sides of the mountains, as well as better irrigation techniques.
mountain_cities: Our cities and fortresses occupy the tops of immense mountains, well past the clouds. They present a formidable obstacle to anyone who might attempt to invade us.
river_trade: The bounty of our great rivers and seas has always fed our people. Let us embrace the river trade, and do what we can to protect the many merchants that travel along the coast to the mouth of the mighty river, so that we may never lack for the fine goods they bring us.
rainforests_and_mountaintops: The rainforests and mountains of our land are teeming with life. Apart from the spirits of the forests, jaguars, anacondas, tarantulas, and a myriad of other animals live among us, and for someone who knows them, they offer little direct danger. To an invading enemy, however, these lands might seem like a fortress and the wild animals as its defenders.
knot_system: By using arrangements of cords and knots to record information, we can greatly facilitate administration of our lands and keeping accurate records of vital information.
llama_farming: Our vast herds of llamas provide us with fabrics to clothe ourselves, meat to feed ourselves, and pack animals to carry our burdens. They are truly invaluable.
mountain_roads: To facilitate easier distribution of goods, a great network of mountain roads connecting far-off valleys together and crossing deep gorges is required. Let us build it.
tears_of_the_sun: Though adventurers from far-off lands dream of finding secret gold on mountain trails high in the Andes, to us the yellow metal has more artistic and sacred importance than simple economic value.
hidden_cities: In a land of immense peaks and impenetrable rainforests, many of our cities are nearly inaccessible to outsiders. They could easily remain hidden for centuries, forgotten by the world.
potato_production: Since maize grows poorly in the high plateaus of our land, we have learned to rely instead on the highly nutritious roots of a local plant. With increased production, we can feed our people and our warriors with this easily maintained crop.
head_hunters: Conquering territory from weaker peoples is a necessary evil in our state. These circumstances have created a unique warrior code, according to which capturing and not killing the enemy is the highest display of bravery and valor. This has made our warriors famous for their mastery in capturing people alive.
border_raiders: Our raiders are famous for their ability to carry out lightning-fast attacks against unaware enemies. Their speed and ability to evade enemy retaliation should be studied and employed by our regular troops as well.
the_sahel_trade: Caravans have been trading between the Sahel and the Mediterranean for ages, the benefits from this trade greatly outweighing the perils of crossing the burning sands of the Sahara.
skilled_cavalry_raids: From the time of our ancestors, horsemen have been the agents of our conquests. The thunder of their hooves ringing across the grasslands of the Sahel spread fear in our enemies, and have brought us many victories.
four_noble_truths: The foundational teachings of the Buddha, the Four Noble Truths explain the reality of being. Nothing is permanent, which causes pain to the spirit, due to its attachment to this transient existence. This spiritual pain can only be eased by liberating oneself from desire and letting go of these attachments, which is achieved by following the Noble Eightfold Path.
noble_eightfold_path: The path to being liberated from Saṃsāra and achieving Nirvāṇa, the Noble Eightfold Path is the purest distillation of Buddhist practices. Dictating both one's mental state and physical actions, it determines proper comportment for any follower of Buddhism.
middle_way: The Buddha teaches us that we should avoid extremes, as neither with sensual indulgence nor extreme asceticism can one achieve enlightenment.
three_jewels: The Three Jewels, or Three Refuges, are the three supports in which a follower of Buddhism takes refuge. These refuges are the Buddha, the enlightened one; the Dharma, the teachings of the Buddha; and the Saṃgha, the monastic community that preserves the Dharma.
buddhist_syncretism: Buddhism has its origins in India, but it has since spread far and wide, coming in contact with many different beliefs. As such, it contains much syncretism not only with the previous Hindu traditions, but with the many other deities it has been exposed to.
sutra: A type of sacred text in both Dharmic and Buddhist religions, they vary in format and content. Regardless, they are always considered to be valid sources of knowledge, and proper study of them is required if one is to develop their spirit.
buddhist_councils: Throughout Buddhist history, monastic councils have discussed canonical texts across different schools. Although the specific form, outcomes, and records of the councils may vary from school to school, the unifying power of such councils — bringing diverse traditions into dialogue — should not be underestimated.
buddhist_canon: Called different names and even containing different texts, depending on the branch of Buddhism, the Buddhist Canon is a collection of sacred Buddhist texts. Containing everything from monastic rules to Sūtra, or teachings of the Buddha, any person dedicated to Buddhism should be familiar with them.
pali_canon: Although there are many different canons in Buddhism, depending on the school, the Theravāda Pāli Canon is the oldest and most prestigious. Other schools have created their canons from a mix of texts with various sources, but the Pāli Canon has remained unchanged since the times of Ashoka 'the Great', and contains the words of the Buddha himself. It has also served as the foundation of many other schools.
buddhist_universities: Since antiquity, Buddhist centers have also been hubs of learning and knowledge, attracting people from all over to study in our institutions. Nālandā was the biggest of these centers in the past, but many others have followed in its footsteps since.
xuanzang_travels: Xuánzàng, a Chinese Buddhist monk who lived during the Táng dynasty in the 7th century, embarked on a seventeen-year overland trip to India in order to visit it centers of learning and to gather a great number of Buddhism texts. Among other places he visited Nālandā, where he learned from the best masters, and on his return to China he brought with him more than a thousand documents, which made a great contribution to Eastern Buddhism. His trip and his records served as basis for the tale of Journey to the West, in which a monk is tasked by the Buddha to travel to India in search of some holy texts. accompanied among others by the Monkey King, Sūn Wùkōng.
silk_road_transmission: It is undeniable the effect that the Silk Road has had on the spread of Buddhism. Whether via land or sea, trade has allowed Buddhism to spread far from its origins in India.
bodhisattva: Regardless of the school of Buddhism one adheres to, a Bodhisattva is an important figure, although their exact characteristics and importance vary between the different traditions. In all cases, however, they are deserving of reverence and admiration.
avalokitesvara: Also known as Guānyīn or Kannon, Avalokiteśvara is one of the most revered Bodhisattvas. Represented as a male or female depending on the school, and even in some considered to be the origin of all Hindu deities, Avalokiteśvara is the Bodhisattva of compassion, and is associated with the mantra Oṃ maṇi padme hūm̐.
maitreya: Maitreya is currently a Bodhisattva, prophesized to be the future and final Buddha of the current era. His destiny is to reestablish the teachings of the Dharma in the world after they have been forgotten by humanity, and as such he is the successor of Siddhārtha Gautama.
mount_meru: Mount Meru is the sacred mountain at the center of the universe in both the physical and spiritual sense for Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism. As it is the center around which everything else revolves, so does our entire country revolve around our ruler.
naraka: Also called Niraya, Naraka refers to the realms of suffering where one's bad karma is cleansed before being reincarnated. There are many Naraka realms, and both the time an individual must reside in them and the punishments they will receive while doing so depends on how much karma they need to gain before being reborn in one of the upper realms.
four_heavenly_kings: Each presiding over one of the cardinal directions, the Four Heavenly Kings are in charge of protecting the Deva realm from the Asuras. They are also responsible for assessing the virtue and morality of mortals.
vegetarianism: Although it depends on the school, there are some rules in the Dharma regarding abstinence from meat consumption. Each school has different views about the strictness of this abstinence, and also whether it should apply only to the monastic community or to the population in general.
edicts_of_ashoka: A legal code published by Emperor Ashoka 'the Great' in the 3rd century BCE, these edicts include strictures promoting for Buddhism. Although this code is from many centuries ago, it still deserves respect and reverence from any member of the Buddhist faithful.
five_precepts: The foundational code of Buddhist ethics and morality, the Five Precepts represent the most basic rules believers must follow in Buddhism, whether part of the ordained monastic community or not. They instruct people to abstain from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxication.
monastic_communities: Buddhist life is centered around its communities of monks and nuns, called the Saṃgha. They are governed by the Vinaya, the rules and precepts that dictate the operations of any Buddhist religious community.
prestigious_schools: Buddhism has developed into a myriad of schools, each one centered around one type of monastic community and declaring a preference for certain texts. However, some of these schools have gained recognition, while others have been relegated to obscurity. Associating with the more prestigious schools gives those people a bit of prestige as well.
offerings: It is a precept of Buddhism to make offerings to the Three Jewels in order to accumulate merit. These offerings may be material or non-material, and some monastic communities depend completely on food donated by their followers for their survival.
incense_burning: The practice of burning incense is a staple of any Buddhist ritual or offering. Varying in shapes and forms, it is common for both lay people and ordained monks and nuns alike to light incense before performing any ritual or meditation. As such, the smell of incense constantly permeates any Buddhist temple.
ascetic_practices: Although the Buddha warned us about the dangers of extreme asceticism, some among the monastic community still perform these strict practices. Limiting the type of cloth they can wear, the food they can eat, or where they can live are some of the restrictions adopted by those who wish to walk this path. Although such abstemious behavior is not a requirement for obtaining merit, it has its own benefits for the practitioner.
mindfulness: An essential part of Buddhist practice, Mindfulness means to be aware of the phenomena of both body and mind, while keeping the teachings of the Buddha always present in the mind. With this, one can avoid the arising of unwanted states, and develop into the wanted ones.
dana: Denoting generosity, Dāna is defined as the act of giving without anything in return, and is a key virtue in all religions related to the Dharma. Helping others selflessly, whereas individually or communally, is one of the key ways of accumulating karma.
ahimsa: The concept of Ahiṃsā, or nonviolence, is a key virtue among all religions following the Dharma. Any conflict is encouraged to be resolved peacefully through dialogue, rather than the use of force. Unfortunately, that is not always possible, but violence should always be the last resort, and its use must be just.
resistance_to_persecution: Although it has spread widely throughout the world, Buddhism has also seen its fair share of persecution across the ages. Its temples and images may have been destroyed, its followers slaughtered or forced into hiding, but nonetheless its faithful have persevered.
buddhist_meditation: Meditation is a common practice among all Buddhist followers, regardless of their school. The aim is to train the mind and the spirit to develop mindfulness, tranquility, and insight, and thus ultimately achieve enlightenment.
res_publica_christiana: We must pursue good relations with our fellow Christian faithful of all denomination, even if we consider some of their practices to be heresy.
roman_orthodoxy: The righteousness of the Roman Catholic faith and its doctrines must remain unquestioned, in order to entrench its authority in the minds of our people.
marian_devotion: Our dedication to the Virgin Mary must remain a central pillar of our worship.
crusading_knights: In this country, we have a long tradition of sending our finest knights and aristocrats to spread the true faith to heathens in the Baltic and Mediterranean regions. We will fulfill our Christian mission by bringing the faith to the unenlightened, while also acquiring experienced commanders for our armies.
catholic_pilgrimages: The holy sites of our faith should be seen by every follower. Encouraging pilgrimages, and elevating those who have undergone the process, should be a priority of our administration.
inquisition_advance: The Inquisition was created in the 12th century as a means to combat the Cathar heresy, but its reach grew significantly in the Late Middle Ages as the main tool of the Catholic Church to counter the spread of dissident doctrines.
preaching_friars: Preaching friars — members of Mendicant Orders like the Dominicans and Franciscans — have taken their ministry beyond the monastery walls to preach directly among the people. By supporting and praising them openly for these acts of devotion, we can strengthen religious conviction throughout the realm, even among the most remote peasants.
devotio_moderna: The Devotio Moderna, or modern devotional movement, is rapidly gaining popularity among members of our faith. We should implement some of their teachings into our court, so as to make ourselves appear particularly devout.
denounce_heretics: We must ensure the supremacy of the one true faith, and denounce all criticisms of it as the bitterest of heresy.
beguins_and_beghards: Many of the faithful have devoted themselves to a life of prayer and good works, which usually comes with taking the veil or becoming a monk. However, they have not taken formal vows, and act without official Roman approval. Nevertheless, we should support these popular efforts to do good deeds and help our people.
conquistador_advance: The discovery of the New World attracts adventurers of all stripes to risk their fortunes and lives on uncertain expeditions, with the promise of unparalleled wealth, fame, and power. These expeditions are formalized through agreements between expedition leaders and the government, legally manifested as 'capitulations of conquest'.
grand_display_of_faith: To honor God, we need to construct great monuments in His name. Not only will this display our devotion to our faith, but it will also demonstrate the magnificent skills of our sculptors and architects.
monastery_productions: The holy occupants of our monasteries are bastions of sensible, frugal living. Our clergy should consider adapting their own lifestyles to more closely resemble those of these monks and nuns.
reform_church_music: We must accept the proposed reforms to our liturgical music. The diluted, soulless tunes currently in fashion can no longer be considered acceptable ways to express the glory of the divine.
frequent_councils: It has been proposed that holding religious councils more frequently would prevent theological disputes and criticisms from festering unchecked. While we may not have full control over the curia, we can at least use our influence to encourage regular synods that address relevant issues before they can become crises.
mendicant_orders: The orders of our faith, who have taken vows of poverty and live itinerant lives, have brought assistance to many remote parts of our country. We should support their efforts as much as we can without disrupting their holy missions.
exsurge_domine: To eradicate the evil of heresy, the Lord Himself will arise and purge them from our lands!
confutatio_augustana: In these turbulent times, we must clearly define orthodox Christian doctrine, while systematically refuting the false beliefs that endanger the very souls of our people.
roman_catechism: Our clergy must adopt the official Roman Catechism as their guide for instruction. This text will improve priestly education and ensure only consistent, orthodox teachings are transmitted to the populace.
oversea_missions: Our clergy is ready and willing to spread our faith into new territories overseas. With their contribution, settling new lands will be made easier and cheaper.
baptism_books: We must confirm baptism as an important cornerstone of our faith by keeping meticulous records of who in our population has or has not yet been baptized.
second_scholasticism: We will need to revive and refine the philosophical movement of medieval scholasticism.
catholic_sunday_schools: Educating the people is an important part of our religious duties. We should establish schools, closely tied to our normal worship services, to provide basic education to our flock.
index_librorum_prohibitorum: The dangerous ideas of the Reformation will spread like a toxic fungus in the minds of our subjects if they have access to written works propagating these silly thoughts! We must forbid certain dangerous texts, and keep a comprehensive list of which books are not allowed.
catholic_cuius_regio_eius_religio: Whose realm, his religion. We will have to accept that other countries follow other faiths, and that this will sometimes be a crucial factor in diplomacy.
embellish_baroque_art: Our faith has a long tradition of sponsoring and promoting great works of art. The development of the splendid new Baroque style reflects the pathos and glory of our theology beautifully, and should receive particular sponsorship.
national_churches: The State must take greater control over the Church in our land. We cannot allow foreign entities to exercise undue influence over our ecclesiastical administration; our Church must serve our realm first.
entrenched_church: No matter which people we rule over, the Church provides a way to give them a unified structure.
catholic_enlightenment: For our faith to withstand the attacks of the Enlightenment, we must adapt, and present new perspectives in and about the Church.
divine_church_music: Many of our composers have created their greatest works thanks to the inspiration provided by their faith. We should actively seek out the most talented artists and hire them immediately so as to never let our churches and cathedrals suffer from inferior music.
continue_missionary_works: Missionary efforts to carry our faith to the far corners of the world can never be considered finished. We need to sponsor more missions to further bring the light of Catholicism to these unilluminated souls.
epic_poetry_advance: For millennia our people have preserved the legends of gods and heroes through epic poetry. Works such as Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, alongside Hesiod's Theogony, stand among the greatest monuments of our cultural heritage. These timeless narratives continue to shape our identity and inspire generations.
makaron_nisoi_advance: The Makaron Nesoi, the Blessed Isles, are believed to be the ultimate destination of the most virtuous souls. Those who live lives of piety and excellence may earn their place among heroic spirits in the Elysian fields. Tales of these sacred realms inspire the pursuit of virtue, honor, and moral excellence throughout society.
religious_dialects_hellenic_faith_advanc: Although our faith is shared across many communities, notable divergence exists in ritual, tradition, and local religious practice. Over time these variations develop organically, sometimes even within the same province. Much like language evolves into regional dialects, our religious customs gradually form distinct local expressions while remaining within the same sacred tradition.
offerings_to_the_moirai_advance: Each year a portion of our ritual offerings is dedicated to the three Moirai, the Fates who govern destiny itself. Clotho the Spinner, Lachesis the Alloter of life's portion, and Atropos the inevitable end preside over the completion of every mortal life according to the cosmic order. In many theological traditions their authority is considered primordial, sometimes even surpassing that of the gods.
on_hubris_and_morality_advance: The principles of our faith originate from the will of the gods and are interpreted through priests, seers, and acts of divination. Through prophecy and sacred interpretation mortals attempt to understand the divine order of the cosmos. Yet the surest path to moral virtue remains piety, reverence, and the careful avoidance of destructive hubris.
variety_in_divine_identity_advance: Our pantheon contains a remarkable variety of deities, each representing different virtues, crafts, and ideals. This diversity allows every individual to discover a divine patron that resonates with their life and vocation. The modest altar of a blacksmith to Hephaestus carries meaning equal to the noble devotion offered to Zeus.
mystai_advance: Hidden behind masks, symbols, and sacred ritual, influential initiates gather within secretive mystery cults. These organizations exercise considerable social and political influence, shaping events through ritual authority, wealth, and discreet alliances. Wise rulers maintain good relations with these mystai, lest their influence and intrigue turn against the state.
preserve_theogony_advance: Hesiod's Theogony recounts the origins and genealogy of the gods, revealing the birth of the divine order itself. Through its verses, symbols of authority such as the scepter and the voice of rule are presented as sacred responsibilities. The work reminds rulers that true authority must be exercised through wisdom, moderation, and reason.
unify_priestly_class_advance: For much of our history the priesthood responsible for sacred lands and temple revenues has functioned in a decentralized manner. Yet recent developments in foreign religious institutions have introduced new ideas of organization and central authority. These influences now encourage the unification and coordination of our own priestly hierarchy.
sruti: Meaning 'that which is heard', Śruti are the holiest and most ancient texts of Hinduism. They are considered to be a divine revelation and thus not attributed to human authorship, although some deny their divine origin while still accepting their authority.
vedah: The main texts among the Śruti are the Vēdaḥ, which are the oldest Sanskrit texts. Their authorship is attributed to Brahmā in the Mahābhārata, and they are the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and the Atharvaveda.
smrti: Meaning 'that which is remembered', Smṛti texts are inspired by or originated from the Vēdaḥ, and thus are considered less authoritative than the Śruti due to being derived from them. However, unlike the Śruti, the Smṛti texts have attributed authorship and are transmitted through manuscripts.
mahabarata: One of the two major Smṛti texts together with the Rāmāyaṇa, the Mahābhārata is an epic of ancient India. It is the longest epic poem ever written, about ten times bigger than the Greek Iliad and Odyssey combined, and it narrates the story of a dynastic struggle for the throne of the ancient Indian kingdom of Kuru culminating in the Kurukshetra War, also called Mahābhārata War. The story ends with the death of Kṛṣṇa and the end of his dynasty.
ramayana: One of the two major Smṛti texts together with the Mahābhārata, the Rāmāyaṇa is an epic of ancient India. It narrates the life of Rāma, avatar of Viṣṇu, as a prince of the kingdom of Kosala. It emphasizes the importance of virtue in all aspects of one's life.
purana: Considered part of the Smṛti, the Purāṇa are texts with a variety of content. Cosmology, divine genealogies, astronomy, grammar, love stories... almost everything can be found within them. As such, even though they are not part of the Śruti, their influence on Hindu beliefs and society is strong, as they combine diverse local beliefs and traditions into the common narrative of the Vēdaḥ.
atman: Referred to the true and eternal unchanging Self, it is the essence of each individual's consciousness. According to the schools, this Ātman is distinct from the mind and body, and it is also different from the Jivātman that persists across multiple lifetimes. In contrast, the schools interpret the concept differently, or reject it entirely.
nastika_schools: Some schools of thought in Hinduism deviate from the mainstream, rejecting the authority of the Vēdaḥ and the existence of Ātman. These schools, like Jainism and Buddhism, are thus heterodox, although they still contain many of the shared core beliefs of Hinduism.
astika_schools: Called the orthodox schools of Hinduism, they accept the authority of the Vēdaḥ and the existence of Ātman. Although consisting of many different branches, this commonality of acceptance gives the Āstika Schools a lot of common ground.
diversity_of_beliefs: The beliefs of the people of India center around the concept of Dharma and the text of the Vēdaḥ, but they are manifested in a myriad of forms and practices. Even the gods recognized and worshiped are not the same for everyone, but a common thread of concepts is present throughout.
ishvara: Interpreted differently depending on the school or branch of Hinduism, Īśvara refers to the Supreme Being or God. Therefore, it can refer to Śiva for Shaivism, to Viṣṇu for Vaishnavism, or to any personal god of the individual.
sanskritization: Hinduism has spread much farther than its origins in India, and many other cultures and countries have adopted Sanskrit concepts and titles to refer to their own identity. As such, the concepts of Hinduism have seamlessly permeated and blended into foreign beliefs.
bhakti_movement: Having emerged in the 6th century, this movement promotes love and devotion to one's personal god or towards an enlightened individual. It appeals to the lay population by speaking to them directly on their own terms. A highly influential movement, it is changing how religion and belief themselves are understood by our people.
yoga: A prominent Hindu school and philosophy, Yoga is a set of practices both physical and spiritual, with the purpose of controlling the mind and body. Performed for millennia, it has almost become synonymous with the path of enlightenment.
diwali: Called the festival of light, Diwali is when we celebrate the triumph of the Dharma; the victory of good over evil and light over darkness. We will light candles and lanterns to symbolize this victory, and we will honor our ancestors.
holi: Held at the beginning of spring to celebrate its arrival, Holi is the festival of colors and love. We commemorate agriculture and good harvests, and at the same time enjoy the myriad of colors that spring offers. It is also the time to have fun and resolve conflicts, removing one's emotional impurities.
holy_rivers: Rivers and their veneration have always been an important part of Hinduism. From the Indus to the Ganges, there are many rivers considered holy, on the shores of which many rituals are held. Their waters are considered sacred, and they are a common site for purification rituals.
advaita_vedanta: Rejecting the dualism between consciousness and matter, Advaita Vedānta claims that the Ātman, or the innermost self or consciousness, is one and the same as the supreme reality or consciousness of the universe, Brahman. In this sense, the physical material world is just an illusion hiding the ultimate reality of the Brahman.
hindu_muslim_relations: There has been a lot of interaction in the past between Hinduism and Islam, and there will continue to be so. Our peoples have learned to live peacefully together and there has even been some degree of syncretism between the two faiths.
hindu_unification: Despite the differences in beliefs and practices throughout Hinduism, there are more commonalities between us than differences. A common unified view of Hinduism has started to emerge, and our people can gain a great sense of unity through it.
hindu_architecture: Regardless of the style of construction, be it a Śikhara, Vimāna, or Prāṅg, Hindu temples are recognizable everywhere for their tall, decorated towers. A representation of Mount Meru, more or less emphasized depending on the region, these spires serve both as a signal of faith and a demonstration of power.
varna_system: Since the times of the Vēdaḥ, there has existed the concept of one's Dharma being classified as one of the four possibles: Brāhmaṇa, scholars or priests; Kṣatriya, rulers or warriors; Vaiśya, farmers or merchants; or Śūdra, artisans or servants. These classifications are not rigid, but instead represent the ideal of an individual's calling, and they have been very influential in Hindu society.
extreme_pacifism: Based on the concept of Ahiṃsā, Hinduism always advocates for pacifism and nonviolence. However, our enemies should still be wary of provoking us, lest we end up exemplifying the complete opposite extreme when roused into war.
hindu_empires: There have been many empires in the past that followed Hinduism. From the Maurya and Gupta empires in India, to the Śrīvijaya Empire in Indonesia, and the long-lasting Chola Dynasty, Hinduism has always been the spirital force behind the throne of powerful rulers.
sacred_cattle: As part of Ahiṃsā, it is prohibited to slaughter cattle. They instead are respected and venerated as maternal figures, and are symbols of selfless provision and sacrifice. Having been worshiped since the time of the Vēdaḥ, they still command enormous respect and attention.
judaism_talmudic_academies: Our great yeshivot inherit the Babylonian academic tradition, transmitting the Talmud and its commentaries through unbroken master-disciple chains across our scattered communities.
judaism_kabbalistic_tradition: The mystical and esoteric current we call Kabbalah interprets the Torah through symbolic frameworks of divine emanation, transmitted in closed lineages alongside the legal halakhic study.
judaism_communal_autonomy: Our communities govern themselves through the kahal, the rabbinic elder council that adjudicates internal religious law, raises communal taxation, and represents our religious people to the host crown.
judaism_court_patronage_finance: Religious-minority status exempts our financiers from the Christian usury prohibitions binding majority counterparts, opening moneylending and mint master niches at every royal court that needs credit.
judaism_tikkun_mysticism: Our mystical school develops the doctrine of Tikkun (cosmic repair), framing the dispersed condition of Jewish as an active spiritual mission to mend a shattered world through prayer, study, and ethical action.
judaism_halakhic_codification: Our jurists organize centuries of accumulated halakhic rulings into structured legal compendia, giving every observant community access to harmonized standards through manuscript and printed networks.
judaism_court_patronage_banking: Our financiers transcend individual royal lending to operate multi-court banking houses simultaneously, leveraging the diaspora as a cross-state credit network no single-religion banking community can replicate.
judaism_rabbinic_council: Leading rabbis of our communities convene a regional council to harmonize halakhic rulings, regulate inter-communal commerce, and represent our religious people before the crown, appointing negotiators and resolving disputes.
judaism_diaspora_communal_institutions: Our communities formalize the Beit Din (the rabbinic court) with codified jurisdiction over marriage, divorce, inheritance, and excommunication, binding our religious community into a coherent legal and spiritual order independent of host tribunals.
judaism_state_credit_apparatus: Our religious banking houses transition into the apparatus of state credit, provisioning entire wars and underwriting peace settlements directly; the host state's fiscal-military capacity becomes inseparable from our religious community's collective creditworthiness.
judaism_hasidic_movement: The popular mystical movement of Hasidism revolves around charismatic tsaddikim who guide their communities through emotional and experiential piety, joyful song, and personal closeness to the divine, reaching the unlettered peasantry that pure textual scholarship cannot.
judaism_rationalist_yeshiva: Our scholarly yeshivot sharpen Talmudic analysis into a precise rationalist method (close textual reading, systematic legal deduction, and rigorous critique), publishing commentary and responsa for the wider observant community.
judaism_religious_emancipation: Absolutist and revolutionary states grant our religious community civic equality, opening guilds, professions, military service, and elective offices that were religiously barred for centuries; our worshippers continue their internal religious life while becoming full subjects of the host state.
judaism_reform_movement: Religious reformers modernize observance by introducing vernacular liturgy, decorum reforms, and theological reinterpretation that aligns religious practice with the bourgeois civic life into which emancipation has placed our religious community.
judaism_international_banking_networks: Our religious banking dynasties (spanning multiple courts through interlocking family banking houses) serve as informal diplomatic conduits between states that cannot openly negotiate, transferring not only funds but messages, terms, and quiet pressure.
judaism_mussar_movement: The Mussar ethical and spiritual movement turns inward, replacing externalized practice with deliberate self-cultivation, character refinement, and meditative ethical discipline as the response to modernization pressures eroding traditional observance.
judaism_modern_orthodoxy: Orthodox observance reconciles itself with secular education, civic participation, and bourgeois life, formulating the principle of religious law within modernity rather than against it, while maintaining strict ritual observance.
judaism_positive_historical_movement: The Positive-Historical religious approach treats halakhic law as historically conditioned but enduringly authoritative, embracing scholarly historical analysis of religious sources while preserving the legal binding of those sources.
second_council_of_ephesus: The Second Council of Ephesus, convened in 449 at the instance of Pope Dioscorus of Alexandria, was a legitimate Christian council despite its denunciation by the Catholic and Orthodox Churches. At this council, the formula of Cyril of Alexandria — which states that Christ is a single incarnate nature, both human and divine — was officially accepted.
rejection_of_chalcedon: As they did not accept the Second Council of Ephesus, the Council of Chalcedon was called at the instance of Pope Leo I, who demanded the nullification of the Second Council of Ephesus. We reject this false council, and stand by the decisions made in the original one.
monophysite_vs_miaphysite: Although Miaphysitism also proclaims that the figure of Christ has only a single nature, it differs substantially from the Eutychian Monophysite view which proclaims that the humanity of Christ was absorbed into his divinity. Though there may be some that also call us followers of Monophysitism, it is just an agreement in words, as in substance our views are clearly different.
original_christianity: There have been many schisms and divisions in the Christian world, but our creed traces its roots on the original true Christianity formulated from the First Council of Nicaea. Every split from the main branch after this is mere heresy.
beyond_the_borders: Christianity undoubtedly originated inside the cradle of the Roman Empire, and many of its branches have been content to stay in that region. Miaphysitism, however, was on the edges of the Empire after being denounced by the Chalcedonians, and has spread far beyond its birthplace, bringing the light of God to the most remote places.
isolated_reaches: Miaphysitism has managed to spread to very distant places. Even while surrounded by enemies and heretics, our faith has remained strong.
independent_leaders: Due to the isolation of Miaphysitism, it has been difficult at times to contact other patriarchates. As such, our leaders have learned to act independently, while at the same time keeping in contact with the rest of the Christian world as much as possible.
jerusalem_focus: We always keep the holy city of Jerusalem in our minds, as not only it was the place where Jesus preached and died, but also where he will return to in his Second Coming. As such, we always pray facing in the direction of Jerusalem, no matter where we are.
acceptance_of_old_testament: Some Christian denominations have decided to reduce the importance of the Old Testament, claiming that the arrival of Jesus completely supersedes it. We, however, maintain that it is still relevant, and that some instructions in it are as valid as they were when they were written.
primacy_of_alexandria: Although Miaphysitism has many branches and independent leaders, we recognize Alexandria and its seat as our spiritual leader. However, this is a sign of respect for the Apostolic Throne and a way to honor it, rather than a bestowal of any special prerogatives.
school_of_alexandria: The Catechetical School of Alexandria, allegedly founded by the Apostle Mark himself, is the oldest school of catechism in the world. There, biblical and theological studies have been taught since the start of Christianity itself. Although the school itself was destroyed when the Bishop of Rome was declared to be above the Patriarch of Alexandria, its tradition has endured.
preserving_of_local_languages: Despite the importance of Greek and Latin in early Christianity, Miaphysitism has preserved its liturgy in more local vernaculars, like Coptic, Aramaic, and Armenian. Venerable languages in their own right, each Miaphysite branch preserves its own historical tongue.
double_patriarchate: Both Alexandria and Antioch see themselves as having two different patriarchates, one for Miaphysitism and another for Orthodoxy. Although they both may claim legitimacy, only Miaphysitism preserves the true patriarchates.
eastern_christianity: We are part of the branch of so-called Eastern Christianity, which amalgamates many different denominations with different theological and liturgical traditions, but also with many common cultural aspects.
life_among_infidels: The lands of the faithful have often been tainted by the presence of unbelievers, but this is why our clerics have ventured forth towards the unknown to bring the light of Jesus to distant lands. We have thus influenced these lost souls in more ways than what one might expect, even if we have not been able to make them see the error of their beliefs.
gradual_departure: Although they were quick to brand us as heretics, Miaphysitism did not cut ties with the rest of the Christian world instantly. We kept in contact with the other patriarchates, and attended the councils, but it was gradually made clear that Miaphysitism is too different from those heretical beliefs.
thrive_under_persecution: Although our faithful have been persecuted by heretics for centuries, our beliefs have persevered. No matter how many times they bring us down, we will rise again!
preserver_of_national_identity: It is because of our history of being persecuted and oppressed that our Church became responsible for preserving our identity. It is in the bosom of the Church where our languages and traditions have been kept safe, and therefore we have unshakeable faith in this institution.
defense_against_heretics: Ever since our split from other Christian faiths, the heretics have come to us with accusations and condemnations many times. They may call themselves Christian, but their views are obviously clouded, whereas our vision is made clear by the light of God.
remote_patriarchates: Conquest and persecution have repeatedly forced our patriarchates to relocate after their seats have fallen under control of heathen conquerors. Though we now operate from new locations, the original seats remain spiritually revered in our tradition, albeit from a distance.
further_reaches: Despite many attempts by nonbelievers to stop our faith from spreading, it has nevertheless made its way to many different peoples and cultures, bringing light wherever it goes.
internal_communion: Despite having independent patriarchs, all branches of Miaphysitism maintain mutual communion. This helps them build relationships with each other, and promotes unity in the Church.
cradle_of_monasticism: Monasticism in Christianity was born in Egypt, when the Christian faithful retreated to the desert to pray and dedicate their lives to God. Miaphysitism can therefore claim this history as their own through the Alexandrine tradition.
unique_architecture: The relative isolation of our patriarchates have resulted in the development of unique architectural styles for our holy places. Although other Christian denominations may be more prominent, our captivating architecture is an inspiration to the faithful.
people_of_allah: We are the followers of Allāh, the only true God, and abide by His Word. All those who believe in Him are our brothers and sisters in His eyes.
holy_revelation: The Word of Allāh was revealed to His Prophet Muḥammad, peace be upon him, and transcribed in the Holy Qur'ān. Through its verses, Allāh's will is passed to His faithful, and all Muslim believers should be familiar with its passages.
islamic_calligraphy: Islam is not only a religion of peace, but of the arts. The calligraphy used to write the verses of the Qur'ān and the names of the prophets often straddles the line between scripture and art.
islamic_prayer: One of the Five Pillars of Islam, Aṣ-Ṣalāh is the obligation for a Muslim faithful to perform daily prayers. Although the number of times one must pray every day and the specific movements when doing it may vary from school to school, the act of daily prayer is common among all Islam.
zakah: One of the Five Pillars of Islam, Al-Zakāh is a form of almsgiving considered a religious obligation for any Muslim faithful. Giving money to help the needy is a mandatory charity for everyone that can afford it, and it is considered a tax.
muslim_lineage: Ever since the times of Muḥammad, peace be upon him, Islam has been intrinsically linked to rulership structures. As such, our dynastic line is also legitimized by the faith itself.
muslim_caravans: From the many paths of the Silk Road, to the salt routes across the Sahara, our people have a tradition of embarking on trade ventures to faraway lands, providing us and the rest of the Muslim world with a wide selection of available goods.
islamic_golden_age: The impact that the Islamic Golden Age had on the entire world, not only in Muslim countries, is absolutely undeniable. Some of these infidel nations are only now emerging from their dark ages of ignorance, making their first attempts at artistic and scientific 'discoveries' that we invented — and perfected — long ago.
ramadan: A commemoration of the first revelation to Prophet Muḥammad, peace be upon him, the month of Ramaḍān is the holiest month in Islam. During this month, all Muslim faithful are expected to perform Ṣawm — fasting and abstinence — during the daylight hours, as well as prayer and reflection.
sunnah: Consisting of the traditions and practices attributed to Muḥammad, peace be upon him, the Sunnah dictates how every Muslim faithful should behave, and is also what gives Sunnism its name. Although the different schools of jurisprudence may vary on the details, they all have their basis in the Sunnah.
imamate: The basis of Shiite faith is that Muḥammad, peace be upon him, designated 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib as his successor. As such, the figure of Imām is that of a spiritual leader coming from the line of Muḥammad, peace be upon him, to lead all Muslim faithful.
islamic_jurisprudence: Centuries of scholarship have matured the science of fiqh and the uṣūl al-fiqh into a complete framework for governing the realm by the Sharī'ah. With the law so thoroughly articulated, the trained jurists who staff our courts can administer the law in its proper way, allowing us to maintain the structures of our government functioning.
indian_sea_trade: Muslim traders have sailed the waters of the Indian Ocean for generations, traveling impossibly far in search of rare and valuable goods. From the eastern coasts of Africa, to the shores of India, and even as far as the spice islands of Indonesia, the waters are crossed by vessels of the Muslim faithful.
muslim_trade_communities: The presence of Muslim traders in faraway lands puts them in contact with many different peoples and beliefs. The establishment of trade communities among them allows for a certain degree of blending and syncretism of their beliefs with the true Word of Allāh.
expansionist_faith: From its origins in Arabia, Islam has expanded far and fast. In a few generations, its believers spanned from Iberia to India, the most rapid religious expansion the world has ever seen. There are new lands waiting to be touched by our light, however — perhaps it is time for a second Muslim expansion.
blend_of_influences: Islam has expanded to many new places since its origins in Arabia, and with this spread, it came into contact with many different peoples and ways of life. Many exchanges of influence happened during this process, to the point that many characteristics not originally part of Islam have become intrinsically associated with the faith.
islamic_schoolars: Islam has always encouraged study and analysis of its scriptures, to the point where we have developed entirely different schools of thought on how to interpret them. Our scholars are therefore extremely learned in the Qur'ān and our other holy texts, capable of having the most in-depth theological discussions.
gunpowder_empires: Gunpowder may have been invented in the Far East, but it was through Islam that it became widely used throughout the world. Gunpowder weapons have been a staple of our armies for generations, and its production and use is one of our defining characteristics.
established_holy_sites: While other religions have somewhat lax and inconsistent views towards how their holy sites are used, the rules of Islam about sacred places are quite clear. Our people will undoubtedly make their pilgrimages with the appropriate reverence and dignity.
islamic_courts: The royal courts of Muslim countries have always been among the most admired in the world. Praised for our refined culture and luxurious appointments, tales of the magnificence of our courts have spread far and wide, and our people take great pride in this reputation.
schools_of_thought: Islam tradition has always emphasized the pursuit of knowledge and education. From schools of jurisprudence and theology to the great libraries and institutions of learning established by various rulers, Muslim scholarship has earned admiration throughout the Muslim world and well beyond.
distant_trade_ventures: It is from the most distant places that the most lucrative trade goods come. For many years, Muslim traders have traveled huge distances both on land and across the seas in search of profitable trade opportunities.
resilient_merchants: Muslim traders endure the harshest of conditions during their expeditions. From crossing the scorching sands of the Sahara and Gobi Deserts, to braving the monsoon-plagued waters of the Indian Ocean, they have proved time and again that they will undergo any hardship in order to bring about successful trade.
jewels_of_the_desert: Islam arose from the sands of Arabia and spread across a largely arid region. Yet some Muslim cities became like prosperous jewels shining in the harsh desert, literal and figurative oasis made bountiful through trade, architecture, and irrigation. With wise investment and planning, any desert settlement can achieve a similar status.
comprehensive_land_survey: In order to know who should pay taxes, we must first know who owns what. A comprehensive land survey, and regularly updating it, are therefore essential. We will always get what we are due!
counting_the_people: Now that we know who owns what, the logical follow-up is to get a clearer idea of who lives where. This will tell us where to look when we need fresh recruits for our armies.
cosmopolitan_court: People from all over admire the beauty and sophistication of our Muslim court. We have therefore become an appealing destination for talented luminaries of all kinds, which only adds to our overall court vibrancy and prestige.
caliphate: The Ḵilāfa, or Caliphate, is the union of all Muslim faithful under a single ruler in the form of the Ḵalīfa, who is to be the political and spiritual successor of Muḥammad, peace be upon him. Although there are different ideas about who is eligible to be Ḵalīfa, the idea of all Islam united under a single banner has always been the primary focus of this process.
ibadi_imamate: Unlike the Ḵilāfa or a divinely appointed Shiite Imām, an Ibadi Imām does not rule over the entirety of the Muslim world, but instead governs locally. Every community can be ruled independently by its own Imām.
contacts_network: The extensive reach of Islam has brought Muslim countries in contact with many different foreign lands. Maintaining a rich network of international contacts such as ours is always beneficial for diplomacy.
infiltration_tactics: Although the ancient Nizārī Shiite order of the Ḥashshāshīyīn has been largely mythicized beyond their original scope, their tactics of subterfuge and assassination were undeniably effective. If we employ such infiltration tactics ourselves, we should benefit from the same success.
unified_armies: It cannot be denied that Islam has spread to many different cultures and peoples since its emergence in Arabia. As long as they believe in Allāh, any person should be able to fight in His name, regardless of their origin.
harsh_environments: Islam has, since its inception, found its way to civilizations in some of the harshest environments of the world. If anyone from outside our region tries to invade our territories, they will find it fiendishly difficult — as they should!
the_pentarchy: The old structure of the Church formulated by Emperor Justinian is still in full effect in Orthodoxy. Although the patriarch of Rome believes himself to be above all else, for the authentic Church, the cities of Constantinople, Alexandria, Antioch, and Jerusalem remain far more important.
imperial_creed: Orthodoxy has been the official faith of the Roman Empire ever since its adoption of Christianity. The heresies of the West and their falsely proclaimed 'emperors' will not be able to discredit our legitimacy.
filioque_issue: The heretical addition of the Filioque clause, which states that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father 'and the Son', was done without calling the appropriate ecumenical council, and therefore it is illegitimate. We are the guardians of the true prayer, and Rome shall be damned for their heresy!
septuagint: Our Old Testament is encoded in Greek, using the version known as the Septuagint, which is a translation from Hebrew done in the 3rd century BC. It was written by seventy-two isolated translators, who all came up with the exact same translations independently. It is thus definitely divinely inspired, and the direct word of God.
anagignoskomena: Our Bible contains all books worthy of veneration and study, even though some may have less importance than others. The Anagignoskomena are not present in the Hebrew Bible, so they receive less attention than other texts, but they are nonetheless worthy of being read and should not be disregarded.
religious_icon_power_advance: Icons are the physical representation of our faith, sacred depictions of holy figures designed to inspire awe and devotion to those that contemplate them.
church_guidance: The Scriptures are the Word of God, but only the Church is able to interpret their correct meaning and to relate it accurately to the flock. Any independent reading or interpretation of the Scriptures outside of Church guidance would only lead to being lost in falsehoods and on the path to heresy.
unchanging_tradition: The tradition passed down to us by Jesus Christ and the apostles is consistent, without any changes, additions, or subtractions whatsoever. Our faith is undeniable in its truths, and what is fundamentally true about this world cannot be changed by mortal hands.
church_councils: As the Church must be united in its judgments, any matter too complex for a single bishop to resolve requires us to call a council, where the bishops will consult the mind of the Church itself. The council's decisions shall therefore reflect the consensus of the Church as a whole.
greek_rite: Our rites and canonical practices have been for centuries well-defined following the Greek rites of Constantinople. Although there may be some small variations in certain places, there is remarkable homogeneity in the rites performed throughout Orthodoxy.
physical_body_of_christ: Our Church is the physical manifestation of the Body of Christ on Earth, having no difference from the one in Heaven. As such, the Church is the physical embodiment of the Lord Savior, sent for the benefit of His people.
sight_veneration: The most important aspect of veneration is the faithful be reminded of great works, miracles, and figures through their natural sense. As such, our churches are adorned with vibrant images and colors, ringing with music and sweetly scented with our holy incense, so that the presence of Christ on Earth can be immediately felt by all inside.
theotokos: The Virgin Mary is a key figure in our beliefs, as she fulfilled the Old Covenant by carrying within her the New Covenant in the figure of Christ. As such, being the bearer of Christ God-incarnate, she was literally the Mother of God, and has a place of prominence above all other saints.
heavenly_architecture: Orthodox religious buildings are designed in imitation of heaven. Their construction centralized around the basilica, the central dome that serves as a roof and symbolizes the heavens. Richly decorated in beautiful images and gleaming golden icons, they are a wonder to behold.
iconostasis: One key feature of any Orthodox church is that of the Iconostasis, a wall of icons that separates the main body of the building from the altar. The icons it contains serve as a visualization of the link between the worshipers and the Holy of Holies, and thus the link between Heaven and the people, serving as a guide for the people towards Heaven.
julian_calendar: The time of our country and our Church has been for centuries measured by the Julian Calendar, promulgated by Julius Caesar in 46 BC. It not only unifies all eastern Christian nations, but it also serves to dictate when the important feasts and celebrations are to be held.
paschal_cycle: Orthodoxy contains some movable feasts around Pascha, Easter, organized in the Paschal Cycle. The ten weeks before Pascha are called Triodion, while the fifty days after Pascha are called Pentekostárion. This cycle marks the most important celebrations in the liturgical year.
oktoechos: An eight-mode system of writing music, the Oktōēchos has been the system used for writing religious chants and music for the Church for centuries. It is the foundation of Orthodox chant, although with some variations between cultures.
prestigious_monasticism: In Orthodoxy, monasticism and asceticism are highly valued and almost a requirement. Any bishop must be a monk first, and they must become a monk before being consecrated if they are not. As such, monasteries and monasticism centers have a big impact on our clerical life.
national_rites: The presence of different autocephalous patriarchates in our Church allows for certain variations between the national rites of each country. However, the unity of the message remains, and the Church as a single entity is not broken.
heirs_of_rome: Many have claimed to be the heirs of Rome and indeed the whole Roman Empire. However, only our religion is the true faith of the old Empire, and therefore only we can legitimately claim to be a direct descendant from it.
legacy_of_saint_andrew: According to legend, Saint Andrew himself visited Scythia and the northern shores of the Black Sea, prophesying a great flourishing of Christianity once he reached the future site of Kyiv.
christianization_of_the_slavs: The people of the Kievan Rus' were among the first of the Eastern Slavic people to accept the light of Christ and convert to Orthodoxy. From there, the faith spread throughout the region.
cyril_and_methodius: Two Byzantine theologians from the 9th century, these men were instrumental to the evangelization of the Slavs. They are credited for developing the Glagolitic alphabet, the first one to ever be used to transcribe Church Slavonic, and their followers later developed the Cyrillic alphabet, naming it after Cyril in his honor.
interaction_between_church_and_state: The patriarchates have absolute authority over their own jurisdictions and those who occupy them. By tying their authority to that of the ruler, we can take advantage of the resources of the Church, and use them to strengthen state authority.
outwards_expansion: It is the holy duty of the Church to bring the light of Christ to the pagan and the infidels. We must go beyond our borders to carry salvation to every lost soul!
justified_holy_wars: We cannot allow heathens and heretics to dictate our actions. It is our holy duty to cleanse the land of their impurity so that the true realm of God can be manifested on Earth.
resistance_to_the_infidels: Our Orthodox brethren have seen themselves at times under the yoke of foreign infidels. However, we have learned to endure such oppression, and even live in peace alongside these infidels.
eastern_ecumenism: Christian denominations from the Oriental Orthodoxy are often confused with Eastern Orthodoxy by the uninitiated. Although they are different from us in many key issues, they are still Christian, and our many commonalities could be used to bring them back to the correct faith.
structured_patriarchates: Our patriarchates have always been well organized and structured, each with its own attributions and delimitations. This allows for a better-functioning Church, which leads to a better-functioning state.
protestant_invite_persecuted: While we have seen the light of the true faith, many of our brethren suffer under the oppressive rule of misguided heathens. We should invite these people to settle in our lands, where they can process their faith without repercussions and, more importantly, contribute to our treasury.
protestant_administration_tax: Previously, the clerics shouldered a significant portion of the tax burden. While some of these structures have been dismantled in the wake of the Reformation, the capable common people are still around, and thus must help make up for that missing clerical revenue.
confessio_augustana: The Reformation gives us the opportunity to define a new creed for our people and, more importantly, to accept critique and make adjustments accordingly.
devotionalism: We must revive Augustinian theology, and recognize that our beliefs are built on the emotions and fervor of the faithful.
protect_the_new_faith: Our religion is beset on all sides by enemies. We will have to defend our rights to our own confession against the Catholic oppressors.
expulsion_of_heretics: The troublesome heretics in our domain could easily foment rebellion against our ruler. It would be better if we redirected them to our overseas colonies instead, where they can cause less trouble.
repurposed_monasteries: Former religious properties seized by the state during our national conversion process can serve us now in new ways, such as centers for production or administration.
involved_laity: With the increased involvement of the laity in the day-to-day administration of our Church, our people have found a more personal connection to the faith itself.
protestant_cuius_regio_eius_religio: Whose realm, his religion. We will have to accept that other countries follow other faiths, and that this will sometimes be a crucial factor in diplomacy.
protestant_painters: The Reformation has given our artists the opportunity to explore new themes, finally freed from the obligatory glorification of God. Hiring more of these artists will reflect well on us, and give us the reputation of being a great patron of the arts.
protestant_sunday_schools: Educating the people is an important part of our religious duties. We should establish schools, closely tied to our normal worship services, to provide basic education to our flock.
protestant_work_ethic: The influence of Puritan and Pietist preachers on the Reformation is undeniable. Their emphasis on virtues like diligence and frugality will help us to foster an industrious and dedicated workforce.
embrace_romanticism: In the wake of the Enlightenment's emphasis on reason, we must not forget the power of emotion and imagination. By embracing Romanticism, which celebrates nature, folklore, and national character, our artists will produce works that stir the soul.
wary_of_heretic_preachers: We will need to be wary of forces trying to convert our people, or seduce them back to our previous faith. By publicly declaring these preachers to be malicious and hostile, we can prepare our people for these interactions and more easily reinforce religious orthodoxy.
protestant_innovation: Since the founding days of our faith, we have emphasized the inherent value of questioning established doctrines and beliefs. We should apply these same ethics to other fields of study.
heian_kyo: The city of Heian-Kyō has been the residence of the Emperor for centuries, and is a center for art and culture. It is there where the lavish court of the Fujiwara flourished, and all the people in Japan looked to it with awe and inspiration. We shall embrace its traditional role, and with our patronage make the culture of our capital flourish once again.
matsuri: Every local shrine and temple has its own festivals and celebrations. The people are always eager to participate, for it is their chance to offer devotion and gratitude towards their local protector Kami.
onmyodo: Coming from China centuries ago, the theories of Yīn and Yáng evolved in Japan into Onmyōdō. Expert practitioners, called onmyōji, deal with the purification and exorcism of evil and vengeful spirits, as well as with divination, astronomy, and the study of nature.
sumo: Derived from an ancient agricultural ritual, in which dances served as prayers for a good harvest, the practice of Sumō has escaped the confines of the court and is now a popular practice among the commoners. It also serves as a form of combat training.
nanto_rokushuu: The temples of Nara have been influential since Buddhism first came from China. The six schools that formed around these temples are a renowned repository of knowledge, especially about the teachings of the Buddha and the various ways of achieving enlightenment. However, they also teach more mundane, but equally valuable subjects, such as how to properly administrate a monastery.
shinbutsu_shuugou: Since Buddhism came to Japan, its teachings have coexisted with the worship of local Kami. This has led to them both blending into a single combined set of beliefs, albeit with distinct ritualistic practices.
honji_suijaku: One of the key practices in Shinbutsu-Shūgō is to identify the local Kami as manifestations of the different Buddha, and the Buddhas as manifestations of the different Kami. In the end, they are one and the same, with core forms or Honji taking on different aspects, or suijaku.
hachiman_worship: Hachiman is one of the most venerated divinities. Originally a deification of Ōjin Tennō, after the introduction of Buddhism he was later also identified as a Bodhisattva. He is the protector of the Imperial line and the tutelary god of the warrior class.
gozan_jissetsu: The 'Five Mountains System' originated in China from state-sponsored Chán Buddhist monasteries, atop the holy mountains that gave the system its name. In Japan, the practice continued in the Kamakura period by the sponsoring of the Zen temples, the Five Mountains of Kyōto and the Five Mountains of Kamakura. By maintaining our sponsorship of such institutions, we can use them to help stabilize our rule.
bodaiji: Since antiquity, our people have venerated our ancestors. The most influential of our rulers erect entire temples, where they will be entombed and then worshiped after death, and where their deeds and words will be remembered for all time.
kagura: Originally sacred ritual dances performed in front of the court by the miko, the shrine maidens, the Kagura also inspired the performance of popular ritual dances all around Japan. These dances have evolved into a myriad of forms, but all of them preserving the tradition and ritual they come from.
obon: One of the most important festivals in our culture, Obon is the time to honor the dead, and our ancestors in particular. During the celebrations, offerings of food and ritual dances are performed. People also light fires and lanterns to guide the souls of the dead back home for the celebrations, and once again back to the land of the dead.
neo_confucianism: Confucianism has a millenary history, and Neo-Confucianism has already existed in Japan for centuries. However, active state involvement and support of the faith will strengthen our authority.
danka_system: For centuries, households in Japan have had close relationships with local Buddhist temples, giving them financial patronage in exchange for the temples taking care of their spiritual needs. Formally enforcing this system will keep our people devoted to the faith, and secure the vital role our religion plays in society.
harae: In our faith, the practice of Harae, or ritual purification, is key to removing all tsumi, sins, and kegare, spiritual uncleanness. Mandating that our population performs the Harae rituals properly and frequently ensures that our country remains spiritually pure.
jisha_bugyou: The administrator and supervisor of all the temples and shrines, the Jisha-Bugyō also oversees the activities these religious institutions perform, making sure that their interests align with those of the government.
kokugaku: Almost since its inception as a country, Japan and Shintō have been influenced by foreign ideas coming from China and Buddhism. A new movement is taking root, claiming that our own national spirit is naturally pure, and that our society must be cleansed of any foreign influences.
home_shrines: Ritual and religious practice have been traditionally relegated to shrines and temples. However, more and more of our people are placing in their homes both local family shrines, called kamidana, to venerate the Kami, and butsudan as Buddhist altars for their ancestors.
fukko_shinto: As people are rejecting foreign influence in our culture, they are also starting to reject the teachings of Buddhist and Confucianism interfering in our faith. Given this emerging demand for doctrinal purity, a formal revitalization of Shintō might be wise.
